title: Mouse Spleen Dissociation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
Protocol ID: MUS-SPL-DIS
Version: v1.2
Author: Dillon Corvino

title: Mouse Spleen Dissociation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 1 – Collection and preparation

Euthanise the mouse by an approved method.

Expose the spleen by opening the abdominal cavity.

Excise the spleen and remove connective tissue & adipose tissue
Place it into a petri dish or 15 mL Falcon tube containing cold PBS or FACS Buffer.

title: Mouse Spleen Dissociation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 2 – Mechanical dissociation

Place a 70 µm cell strainer over a 50 mL Falcon tube.

Transfer the spleen onto the strainer.

Using the back of a 5 mL syringe plunger, gently mash the spleen through the mesh until a homogenous suspension is obtained.

Rinse the strainer with FACS Buffer and top the tube up to 50 mL.







Note



Max of 2 spleens per tube/strainer

title: Mouse Spleen Dissociation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 3 – Wash and centrifugation

Centrifuge the 50 mL tube at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.

Carefully pour off the supernatant.

title: Mouse Spleen Dissociation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 4 – RBC lysis

Add RBC lysis buffer to the cell pellet (1 mL per spleen):

ACK lysis buffer: incubate for 1.5–2 minutes at room temperature, or

HybriMax RBC Lysis Buffer: incubate for 4–5 minutes at room temperature.


Gently resuspend immediately by pipetting or flicking to ensure uniform lysis.

Quench the reaction by topping up to 50 mL with FACS Buffer.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.







Warning



Do not exceed the indicated incubation times. Over-incubation is the most common cause of reduced leukocyte viability. If red cells remain, repeat a short second lysis rather than extending the incubation.








Note



ACK lysis buffer is stronger and faster but less forgiving. HybriMax is milder and preferred when viability is critical (e.g. downstream scRNA-seq or adoptive transfer).

title: Mouse Spleen Dissociation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 5 – Filtration and final wash

Filter the suspension through a fresh 70 µm strainer into a clean tube.

Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.

Carefully discard supernatant.

Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL FACS Buffer (or a volume appropriate for your downstream assay).

title: Mouse Spleen Dissociation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 6 – Downstream handling
Proceed immediately to:

Flow cytometry staining

FACS sorting

Cryopreservation

Functional assays

Keep cells on ice until use.

title: Mouse Lung Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
Protocol ID: MUS-LNG-DIG
Version: v1.1
Author: Dillon Corvino

title: Mouse Lung Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 1 – Lung collection

Euthanise the mouse using an approved method.
Open the thoracic cavity to expose the lungs.
(Optional but recommended) Perfuse via the right ventricle with cold PBS until lungs visibly blanch, reducing RBC content.
Excise the entire lung block and place it in a 10 cm petri dish containing cold PBS or FACS/MACS Buffer.







Tip



Perfusion markedly improves final leukocyte purity and reduces RBC lysis requirements.

title: Mouse Lung Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 2 – Tissue mincing

Blot the lungs briefly on sterile tissue to remove excess fluid.
Transfer to a fresh 10 cm dish and mince thoroughly using scissors or scalpels until small fragments are obtained.
Transfer the minced lung into a 50 mL Falcon tube containing 5 mL Lung Digestion Buffer (see buffer protocol BUF-LNG-DIG-v1.0).

title: Mouse Lung Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 3 – Enzymatic digestion

Place tubes on a 37 °C benchtop shaker at 250 rpm.
Incubate for 30–35 minutes.







Warning



Over-digestion can decrease viability and negatively impact epithelial and myeloid populations.

title: Mouse Lung Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 4 – Mechanical dissociation

After digestion, add FACS/MACS Buffer to bring total volume to 25 mL.
Pour the suspension onto a 70 μm cell strainer placed on a 10 cm dish.
Mechanically mash the digested lung through the mesh using the back of a 5 mL syringe plunger.
Rinse the strainer with cold FACS/MACS Buffer until no visible tissue remains.
Transfer the filtered cell suspension back into a 50 mL tube.
Top up to 50 mL with cold FACS/MACS Buffer.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Carefully discard the supernatant.

title: Mouse Lung Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 5 – RBC removal (if required)
Lung digests vary in RBC content. If erythrocytes are visible:

Add 1 mL 1× RBC Lysis Buffer (e.g. HybriMax) per lung.

Mix gently and incubate for 3–5 minutes at room temperature.
Immediately top up to 50 mL with cold FACS/MACS Buffer.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant.







Note



If the lung was perfused effectively, this step may not be needed.

title: Mouse Lung Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 6 – Final wash and resuspension

Loosen pellet by gentle flicking or brief vortexing.
Resuspend in 5 mL FACS/MACS Buffer (or other desired volume).
Filter again through a fresh 70 μm strainer if clumping is observed.
Keep the suspension on ice until staining, sorting, or single-cell workflows.

Vero Cell Seeding

Tip



Aim for evenly distributed, healthy monolayers. Avoid overconfluency and large areas of cell-free plastic.

2% methylcellulose or 2% agarose (cooled to ~42–45°C for agarose)

to obtain a final 1× medium with 1% methylcellulose or 1% agarose.
Prepare and keep overlay medium warm (37–42°C) until use.

title: LCMV Infection Models (WE, Clone 13, Docile, Armstrong)
text:
Protocol ID: MUS-INF-LCMV
Version: v1.2
Author: Dillon Corvino

title: LCMV Infection Models (WE, Clone 13, Docile, Armstrong)
text:
Virus stock handling and preparation
LCMV-WE, LCMV-Clone 13, LCMV-Docile, and LCMV-Armstrong virus stocks are propagated and titrated as previously described in the literature and the LCMV production protocol in this library.

Virus stocks are stored at −80 °C in single-use aliquots.
Repeated freeze–thaw cycles must be avoided.


Thawing

Virus aliquots are rapidly thawed immediately before use.
Thawing is performed in a 37 °C water bath until the aliquot is just thawed.
Aliquots are removed promptly from the water bath and placed immediately on ice.
Virus is kept on ice during dilution and injection.
Repeated freeze–thaw cycles must be avoided.



Dilution buffer

Virus stocks are diluted in sterile, endotoxin-free PBS.
No serum or supplements are added unless explicitly required by internal SOP.
Dilutions are prepared fresh on the day of infection.

title: LCMV Infection Models (WE, Clone 13, Docile, Armstrong)
text:
Infection doses and routes
Mice are infected intravenously (i.v.) via the lateral tail vein using the following standard doses:

LCMV-Clone 13: 2 × 10⁶ plaque-forming units (PFU)
LCMV-WE: 2 × 10⁴ plaque-forming units (PFU)
LCMV-Armstrong: 2 × 10⁴ plaque-forming units (PFU)
LCMV-Docile: 2 × 10^6 plaque-forming units (PFU)







Note



LCMV-Armstrong — route note: The dose used here for Armstrong is 2 × 10⁴ PFU i.v.. The broader literature typically uses 1 × 10⁴ – 2 × 10⁵ PFU administered intraperitoneally (i.p.) for acute infection and memory studies. The i.p. route is the most common in published Armstrong protocols. The i.v. route used here differs from the literature standard — this should be noted when comparing outcomes across studies.



Injection parameters

Injection volume: 200 µL per mouse
Syringe: insulin syringe
Needle gauge: 27G–30G
Injections are performed slowly to ensure proper intravenous delivery.
Successful i.v. injection is confirmed by lack of resistance and absence of subcutaneous bleb formation.

title: LCMV Infection Models (WE, Clone 13, Docile, Armstrong)
text:
Post-infection monitoring

Body weight and general health are monitored daily during the first week post infection.
Monitoring frequency is adjusted according to infection severity and institutional guidelines.
Humane endpoints are applied as defined in approved protocols.

title: LCMV Infection Models (WE, Clone 13, Docile, Armstrong)
text:
LCMV-WE (2 × 10⁴ PFU i.v.)

NLCs accumulate prominently in the liver.
Peak frequency occurs at approximately day 7 post infection.
Elevated NLC levels are maintained through at least day 30 post infection.
This model supports both early and long-term NLC analyses.

title: LCMV Infection Models (WE, Clone 13, Docile, Armstrong)
text:
LCMV-Clone 13 (2 × 10⁶ PFU i.v.)

NLCs peak early, around day 5 post infection.
A sharp contraction occurs by ~day 7, followed by gradual decline through day 30.
The effective experimental window for NLC analysis is day 4–7 post infection.
Sampling outside this window will substantially underestimate NLC abundance.

title: LCMV Focus-Forming Assay (Immunofocus)
text:
Vero cell maintenance

Maintain Vero cells in Vero propagation medium (see buf_vero_propagation_medium.qmd) and passage every 2–3 days when cells reach ~60–80% confluence.
For routine splitting:

Aspirate medium.
Wash with ~10 mL PBS.
Add 5–7 mL trypsin-EDTA and incubate at 37°C for 5 min, monitoring under the microscope until cells detach.
Neutralize trypsin with 20–30 mL Vero propagation medium.
Collect cells into a 50 mL tube and centrifuge at 20°C, 10 min, 400-500g.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend the pellet in an appropriate volume (e.g. 5–10 mL) of fresh medium.
Seed into flasks/plates at the desired density for continued expansion.

title: LCMV Focus-Forming Assay (Immunofocus)
text:
Cell seeding for FFA
Two seeding strategies are described below. The default method seeds Vero cells the day before infection to form an adherent monolayer. The alternative method seeds Vero cells as a suspension immediately before infection, as described in the collaborator protocol.

Default method (recommended): Day −1 monolayer seeding

One day before infection (Day −1), prepare a single-cell suspension of Vero cells from a near-confluent flask.
Count cells using a hemocytometer or automated cell counter.
Dilute cells in Vero propagation medium to reach 70–90% confluence in 24-well plates on the day of infection (Day 0). As a starting point:

Aim for ~1–2 × 10^5 cells per well in 24-well plates.

Seed cells in 24-well incubation plates (e.g. 0.5–1 mL per well).
Incubate overnight at 37°C, 5% CO₂ in the infectious incubator.



Alternative method: Same-day seeding and infection (suspension-based)
This method is based on the collaborator’s protocol and may be useful when a tightly controlled cell number per well is desired.

On Day 0, detach Vero cells from a near-confluent flask as described under maintenance.
Resuspend cells in Vero propagation medium and count.
Calculate total cell number in the suspension. For example, if a counted sample corresponds to N cells per defined volume, determine the concentration and total cells in the resuspension volume.
Dilute the cell suspension to 8 × 10^5 cells/mL in Vero propagation medium.
Keep the cell suspension on ice until seeding.
For each well of the 24-well incubation plate, add 200 µL of this suspension (→ 1.6 × 10^5 cells per well).
Proceed directly with virus addition and infection as described in the infection section.







Tip



The monolayer (Day −1) method may provide slightly more uniform adherence, while the same-day suspension method offers tightly controlled cell numbers per well. Choose one approach and use it consistently within a given experiment.

2% methylcellulose

Prepare a 2% (w/v) methylcellulose solution by dissolving 20 g methylcellulose in 1 L dH₂O.

Do not invert or vortex vigorously, as this can introduce bubbles.

title: Mouse Blood Processing to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 1 – Blood collection

Prepare EDTA-containing microcentrifuge tubes (20–40 µL EDTA per tube) and label one tube per mouse.
Collect blood using an insulin syringe (or other approved method, e.g. retro-orbital, submandibular, cardiac puncture as per ethics approval).
Immediately dispense the blood into the EDTA tube.
Flick the tube gently to mix blood with EDTA and prevent clotting.







Warning



Ensure local ethics approval covers the chosen blood collection method. Handle sharps carefully and discard immediately into an approved sharps container.

title: Mouse Blood Processing to Single-Cell Suspension
section: STEP 2 – Allocate sample volume and Serum removal
text:
STEP 2 – Allocate sample volume and Serum removal

Transfer a defined volume of well-mixed whole blood (e.g. 100–200 µL, or as required) from the EDTA tube into a new, labelled microcentrifuge tube.

Record the volume used per sample in your lab notebook.

Centrifuge the whole blood at maximum g (bench-top microcentrifuge) for 5 minutes at room temperature or 4 °C.
Carefully remove the serum:

Discard, or
Aliquot and freeze at −20 °C or −80 °C if required for serum analyses.

title: Mouse Blood Processing to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 3 – RBC lysis

Gently resuspend the remaining blood pellet in 1 mL of 1× BioLegend RBC lysis buffer.

Transfer the suspension to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Gently mix by inversion or brief pipetting to ensure complete resuspension.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.







Warning



Do not exceed the recommended lysis time; prolonged exposure to RBC lysis buffer can damage leukocytes and alter marker expression.

title: Mouse Blood Processing to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 4 – Wash and final resuspension

After the 5-minute lysis, top up the tube to 10 mL with FACS Buffer.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 4–5 minutes at 4 °C.
Carefully pour off or aspirate the supernatant.
If substantial red cell contamination remains:

Repeat the RBC lysis step (STEP 3) once more, followed by the wash in STEP 4.

Finally, resuspend the cell pellet in an appropriate volume of FACS Buffer (e.g. 0.5–1 mL) for:

Flow cytometry staining
Cell counting
Other downstream assays


Keep the cell suspension on ice until staining.

text:

Version: v1.1
Author: Dillon Corvino

title: Isolation of Human PBMCs from Whole Blood by Ficoll Gradient
section: Step 1 – Tube labelling and blood dilution
text:
Step 1 – Tube labelling and blood dilution

Label 50 mL conical tubes for each blood sample.
For each sample, add whole blood to a 50 mL tube:

Transfer up to 17.5 mL whole blood per 50 mL tube.

Dilute blood 1:2 with R0 medium (RPMI without FCS; BUF-R0-MED):

Add 17.5 mL R0 to 17.5 mL blood (total 35 mL).

If using less than 17.5 mL blood, top up to 35 mL with R0.








Note



Dilution with R0 reduces viscosity, improves layering on Ficoll, and can improve separation quality.

title: Isolation of Human PBMCs from Whole Blood by Ficoll Gradient
section: Step 2 – Ficoll layering and gradient centrifugation
text:
Step 2 – Ficoll layering and gradient centrifugation

In a fresh 50 mL tube, add 10 mL Ficoll (density gradient medium).
Using a 10 mL serological pipette, slowly overlay the 35 mL diluted blood onto the Ficoll:

Hold the Ficoll tube at a gentle angle.
Carefully dispense the diluted blood onto the Ficoll surface, avoiding mixing.
Maximum volume of diluted blood per tube: 35 mL.

Prepare all Ficoll gradients required and ensure they are balanced.
Centrifuge at 450 g (rcf) for 30 min at room temperature with:

Acceleration: 2

Deceleration: 1 (minimal brake)

During centrifugation, prepare 10 mL tubes containing 3 mL R0 (2 tubes per Ficoll gradient) for PBMC collection.

title: Isolation of Human PBMCs from Whole Blood by Ficoll Gradient
section: Step 3 – Harvest of PBMC layer and first wash
text:
Step 3 – Harvest of PBMC layer and first wash

After centrifugation, identify:

Plasma / diluted medium layer on top.
A white, “fluffy” PBMC layer at the plasma/Ficoll interface.
Ficoll layer.
Pellet of erythrocytes and granulocytes at the bottom.

Using a sterile transfer pipette, gently harvest the PBMC layer:

Carefully aspirate the interface and transfer to a 10 mL tube containing 3 mL R0.
Continue until the visible fluffy layer is removed.

For each gradient, distribute the collected PBMCs across two 10 mL tubes (each with 3 mL R0).
Centrifuge the 10 mL tubes at 400 g for 10 min at room temperature:

Acceleration: 9

Deceleration: 9

Carefully remove and discard the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellets.

title: Isolation of Human PBMCs from Whole Blood by Ficoll Gradient
section: Step 4 – Second wash and resuspension in R10
text:
Step 4 – Second wash and resuspension in R10

Resuspend each PBMC pellet in 3 mL R0.
Combine two pellets into one tube and top up to 10 mL R0.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min at room temperature:

Acceleration: 9

Deceleration: 9

Remove and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL R10 (complete RPMI with 10 % FCS; BUF-R10-MED).
If multiple gradients were processed for the same sample, combine their PBMC pellets into a single tube in R10.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1–10 mL R10, depending on pellet size and planned downstream use.

title: Isolation of Human PBMCs from Whole Blood by Ficoll Gradient
text:
Step 5 – Counting and cryopreservation (optional)

Mix the cell suspension gently and take a small aliquot for counting with trypan blue or an equivalent viability dye.
Calculate the total number of viable PBMCs.
For cryopreservation, aim for a final concentration of 10 × 10⁶ cells/mL per cryovial.


5.1 Preparation of 2× freezing medium (BUF-FREEZE-MIX)

Prepare 2× freezing medium by mixing:

7 mL R0

1 mL FCS

2 mL DMSO
(Final: R0 + 10 % FCS + 20 % DMSO; 2× relative to standard 10 % DMSO freezing medium.)

Keep the 2× freezing medium on ice and protected from light.



5.2 Adjust cell concentration and freeze

Adjust PBMCs in R10 to 20 × 10⁶ cells/mL:

If only one cryovial is needed, pellet cells at 200 g for 5 min, remove supernatant, and resuspend so that the cell pellet is in 500 µL R10 (20 × 10⁶ cells/mL).

Add an equal volume of 2× freezing medium (BUF-FREEZE-MIX) to the cells:

Final concentration: 10 × 10⁶ cells/mL in 10 % DMSO.

Gently mix to avoid bubbles.
Dispense 1 mL of cell suspension into pre-cooled cryovials, labelled with:

Patient name or anonymised ID.
Sample type (PBMC).
Date.

Place cryovials into a pre-cooled controlled-rate freezing container (e.g. Mr Frosty) and transfer to a −70 °C or −80 °C freezer.
After at least overnight freezing, move cryovials to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage.

title: KHYG-1 Cell Line Culture Protocol
text:
Step 1 – Medium and reagent preparation

Prepare KHYG-1 complete medium based on R10 (BUF-R10-MED):

RPMI 1640

10% heat-inactivated FCS

1% Pen/Strep


Prepare IL-2 stock according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Immediately before use, supplement complete medium with IL-2:

Final concentration: 100–200 IU/mL (use a lab-validated concentration consistently).

Pre-warm:

KHYG-1 complete medium + IL-2

PBS (if washing is needed)
to 37 °C.








Note



IL-2 should not be stored long-term in medium; add fresh to pre-warmed R10 immediately before feeding or splitting cultures.

title: KHYG-1 Cell Line Culture Protocol
text:
Step 2 – Thawing KHYG-1 cells

Remove a cryovial of KHYG-1 cells from liquid nitrogen and immediately place it in a 37 °C water bath.
Gently swirl the vial until only a small ice crystal remains (1–2 min).
Disinfect the outside of the vial with 70% ethanol and transfer to a biosafety cabinet.
Transfer the vial contents to a 15 mL tube containing 9–10 mL pre-warmed KHYG-1 complete medium without IL-2 to dilute DMSO.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at room temperature.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant without disturbing the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet gently in 10–15 mL pre-warmed KHYG-1 complete medium with IL-2.
Transfer cells to an appropriate flask (e.g. T25 or T75).
Place the flask in a 37 °C, 5% CO₂ incubator.







Warning



Do not leave cells in freezing medium (DMSO-containing) after thawing. Wash promptly to minimise DMSO toxicity.

title: KHYG-1 Cell Line Culture Protocol
text:
Step 3 – Routine culture and passaging

Recommended density range

Maintain cultures between approximately 2 × 10⁵ and 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL.



Monitoring and splitting

Gently resuspend the culture by pipetting up and down or gently swirling the flask.
Remove a small aliquot for counting and viability assessment.
If the cell density exceeds 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL, split the culture:

Remove a defined volume of culture (e.g. half to three-quarters of the flask volume).
Replace with an equal volume of fresh pre-warmed KHYG-1 medium with IL-2.
This corresponds to approximately a 1:2–1:4 split, depending on growth.

Aim to re-establish cultures at 2–3 × 10⁵ cells/mL after splitting.
Return flasks to the incubator (37 °C, 5% CO₂).



Medium change for lower-density cultures

If cells are at acceptable density but medium appears acidic or exhausted:

Gently resuspend cells.

Transfer to a 15 mL tube and centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min.

Aspirate supernatant and resuspend in fresh medium with IL-2 at the desired density.

Return to flask and incubator.








Note



Maintain consistent IL-2 concentrations at each passage and medium change. Record IL-2 lot numbers for traceability.

title: KHYG-1 Cell Line Culture Protocol
section: Step 4 – Short-term maintenance and experimental setup
text:
Step 4 – Short-term maintenance and experimental setup

For experiments, seed KHYG-1 cells at a defined density consistent with experimental requirements (e.g. 2–3 × 10⁵ cells/mL).
Use fresh medium with IL-2 on the day before and the day of the experiment to ensure cells are in active growth phase.
Avoid using cultures older than a defined passage number (e.g. >20–25 passages post-thaw) for critical experiments; restart from frozen stock as needed.

title: KHYG-1 Cell Line Culture Protocol
text:
Step 5 – Cryopreservation of KHYG-1 cells

Freezing medium

Standard freezing medium for KHYG-1:

90% FCS + 10% DMSO
or

Cell suspension in R10 mixed 1:1 with BUF-FREEZE-MIX (2× freezing medium) to yield final 10% DMSO.




Freezing procedure

Ensure KHYG-1 cells are in exponential growth phase (healthy, non-overgrown cultures).
Transfer the culture to a 15 or 50 mL tube and centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and gently resuspend the pellet in freezing medium at 5–10 × 10⁶ cells/mL.
Aliquot 1 mL of cell suspension per labelled cryovial (include cell line name, passage number, date, and your initials).
Place vials into a controlled-rate freezing container (e.g. Mr Frosty).
Freeze at −70/−80 °C for at least 12–24 hours.
Transfer vials to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage.







Warning



Avoid extended handling of cells at room temperature in freezing medium; DMSO is toxic and should be minimised outside of the controlled freezing process.

title: Standard Flow Cytometry Staining (Surface, Intracellular, Intranuclear)
text:
Protocol ID: GEN-FLOW-STD
Version: v1.4
Author: Dillon Corvino

title: Standard Flow Cytometry Staining (Surface, Intracellular, Intranuclear)
text:
Step 1 – Plate setup and buffers

Prepare buffers:

FACS buffer (PBS + 2% FCS) — use only if tetramers are included
MACS buffer (PBS + 2% FCS + 2 mM EDTA) — default buffer

Prepare single-cell suspensions.
Count cells and adjust concentration to plate 2 × 10⁵ – 1 × 10⁶ cells per well.
Aliquot cells into a 96-well U- or V-bottom plate.
Keep plates on ice or at 4 °C.

title: Standard Flow Cytometry Staining (Surface, Intracellular, Intranuclear)
text:
Step 2 – Surface staining (with live/dead ± tetramers)
Surface staining is performed in a single master mix.

If tetramers are included → use FACS buffer (no EDTA)

If no tetramers are included → use MACS buffer

Antibody titration guidance (applies to all surface staining): - Surface antibodies: default 1:200 if titration data are unavailable. - Transcription factors or weakly expressed markers: default 1:50.

2.1 Prepare surface staining master mix
Prepare a 1× surface staining master mix in the appropriate buffer containing:

Fc block: 1:100
Live/dead dye (1× final concentration)
Surface antibodies (1× final concentration)
Optional: Tetramer(s), per manufacturer recommendation

Final volume: 50 µL per well






Note



When tetramers are included, staining is performed in FACS buffer without EDTA to avoid potential interference with multimer–TCR interactions.
Whether EDTA exclusion is strictly necessary remains under investigation and will be empirically evaluated within the lab.








Tip



After flicking off the supernatant, residual liquid in the dead volume can be used to resuspend cell pellets by briefly vortexing the plate at low speed to agitate the wells. This helps achieve uniform resuspension before adding the next reagent.




2.2 Staining

Resuspend each cell pellet in 50 µL surface staining master mix.
Incubate for 30 min on ice, protected from light.



2.3 Wash steps

Top up each well to 200 µL with MACS buffer.
Centrifuge at 1000 g for 2 min at 4 °C.
Flick off the supernatant.
Wash once more with 200 µL MACS buffer, centrifuge at 1000 g for 2 min at 4 °C, and flick.







Note



All antibodies and tetramers should be titrated for optimal performance. Default dilutions are provided as a starting point only.




2.4 Surface staining only

Resuspend pellets in 100–200 µL 4% PFA in PBS.
Wrap the plate in aluminium foil to protect from light and clearly label with name and date.
Store at 4 °C, protected from light, until acquisition.

title: Standard Flow Cytometry Staining (Surface, Intracellular, Intranuclear)
text:
Step 3 – Fixation and permeabilization
This step assumes use of: - BD Cytofix/Cytoperm (cytoplasmic targets), or
- eBioscience FOXP3 fix/perm (intranuclear targets).

3.1 Initial fixation/permeabilization

Add 100 µL fix/perm solution per well.
Incubate 20 min on ice, protected from light.
Top up to 200 µL with 1× PermWash.
Centrifuge at 1000 g for 2 min at 4 °C and flick.
Resuspend in 200 µL PermWash.
Centrifuge at 1000 g for 2 min at 4 °C and flick.



3.2 Optional pause point

Resuspend pellets in 200 µL MACS buffer.
Wrap the plate in aluminium foil to protect from light and clearly label with name and date.
Store at 4 °C overnight, protected from light.







Note



If the protocol is paused at this step, the recovery steps below must be performed before proceeding to intracellular or intranuclear staining.




3.3 Restarting the protocol after pause point

Centrifuge the plate at 1000 g for 2 min at 4 °C.
Flick off the supernatant.
Resuspend pellets in 200 µL PermWash.
Incubate for 30 min on ice, protected from light.
Centrifuge at 1000 g for 2 min at 4 °C and flick.
Proceed directly to Step 4 – Intracellular or intranuclear staining.

title: Standard Flow Cytometry Staining (Surface, Intracellular, Intranuclear)
text:
Step 4 – Intracellular or intranuclear staining

Prepare an intracellular or intranuclear antibody master mix in the appropriate PermWash buffer (kit-specific):

Final volume: 50 µL per well

Resuspend each cell pellet in 50 µL of the antibody master mix.
Incubate 30 min on ice, protected from light, or incubate overnight at 4 °C.







Tip



For intranuclear targets (e.g. FOXP3, Helios, T-bet, Eomes), overnight antibody incubation at 4 °C can improve signal intensity, particularly for low-abundance or epitope-masked transcription factors.
Ensure plates are well sealed, clearly labelled, and protected from light during overnight incubation.








Warning



Overnight antibody incubation is not recommended for cytoplasmic intracellular targets (e.g. cytokines, granzymes, perforin). Prolonged incubation can increase background staining and does not typically improve signal for these antigens. Use 30–60 min incubations for intracellular (non-nuclear) targets.



Top up each well to 200 µL with PermWash.
Centrifuge at 1000 g for 2 min at 4 °C and flick off the supernatant.
Wash once more with 200 µL PermWash, centrifuge at 1000 g for 2 min at 4 °C, and flick.
Resuspend each pellet in 100–200 µL 4% PFA in PBS.
Wrap the plate in aluminium foil to protect from light and clearly label with name and date.
Store at 4 °C, protected from light, until acquisition.

section: A. Startup and (when required) daily QC
text:
A. Startup and (when required) daily QC






NoteWhen to run daily QC



On weekdays, FCCF staff typically perform daily QC by 09:00. Run the daily QC yourself if: - you start before FCCF operating hours, or - you use the machine on weekends.



Check the left side of the instrument and ensure both black switches are on.
Check Waste and Sheath tank levels. If necessary:

Empty waste into sink, then add 2 pumps of Mucocit® T to the empty waste tank.
Refill Sheath tank with MilliQ water.

Press the Power button on the front of the instrument (green light should turn on).
Turn on the computer.
Log in with your FCCF account.
Start the ID7000 software (desktop icon).
Log into the software.

If using a shared lab account containing saved controls, log into that account (as applicable).

Confirm the ID7000 connects to the computer (bottom right of software). Wait a couple of minutes.
The Priming Wizard should open automatically. Click Start.
While priming runs, prepare QC beads in FACS tubes:

AlignCheck beads: 450 µL FACS Flow + 2 drops beads
Sony 8-peak beads: 350 µL FACS Flow + 1 drop beads

When priming is complete, close the QC window if it pops up.
Click Start Daily and Performance QC.
Open the instrument door.
Remove Clean and Rinse tubes from the tube station.
Place AlignCheck and 8-peak bead tubes into the tube station in the order shown in the QC window.
Close the door and follow prompts to run QC.







TipIf QC fails due to pressure



A pressure-related error can cause QC failure. Re-check Waste and Sheath tank levels and correct if needed, then re-run QC.

title: Sony Spectral Cell Analyzer ID7000
text:
B. Experiment setup

After QC passes, go to Experiment tab.
Click Experiment designer.
Confirm required laser lines are enabled (checkmarks). Enable if needed:

355 nm
405 nm
488 nm
561 nm
637 nm

Add fluorochromes (e.g., FITC, APC, PE) by typing and clicking Add.







NoteOrder of fluorochromes




If acquiring single stains in tubes, fluorochrome add-order does not matter.
If acquiring single stains in a plate, match fluorochrome order to the plate layout.
If using previously saved single-stain controls from the library and no new controls are needed, you may skip Section C.




Fill in metadata (Marker, Species, Clone, Lot number, etc.).
Click Next until Instrument Settings step.
Click Import and import:

Desktop -> Import Master Setting -> SONY_Master Settings normal.xml

Click Next and select acquisition order: From left-to-right.
Click Next and complete experiment details.
Click Create Experiment.
Under Acquisition tab, click Layout Editor (Plate section).
Hold Ctrl and select the unassigned positions corresponding to the number of samples.
Set Sample Group to Sample Group - 1.
Optionally check Auto acquisition target.
Name each sample position under Sample Information.
Close Layout Editor.

title: Sony Spectral Cell Analyzer ID7000
section: C. Acquire single stains and perform unmixing
text:
C. Acquire single stains and perform unmixing

C1. Load single stains

If using tubes:

Retrieve the 24-position 5 mL tube rack from FCCF fridge.
The notch marks A1.

Arrange single-stain tubes (or plate) in the order shown in the software layout.







NoteArC beads for fixable viability dyes



If using ArC beads stained with a fixable amine-reactive viability dye, also add unstained ArC beads as a separate tube. In the software: - Acquisition -> Layout Editor -> select tube position - Name it (e.g., “Unstained ArC beads”) - Under Sample Settings: - Sample Group: Single Positive Controls - Check Auto acquisition target



Open door, orient rack/plate with A1 notch at bottom left, place on AutoSampler.
Close door and click Load.

If “Cooling sample stage is in progress” appears, click Yes.




C2. Instrument settings for single stains (example values)

Open Instrument Settings.
Under Detector and Threshold:

FSC Gain = 17 (example for fixed/permeabilized PBMCs)
SSC Voltage (%) = 37.5 (example for fixed/permeabilized PBMCs)

Under Flow Control:

Sample Flow Rate = 3.0








NoteAdjust for your sample type



The FSC/SSC and flow rate values above are examples given for fixed/permeabilized PBMCs. Adjust for other cell types and staining conditions.




C3. Stopping condition for single stains

Open Stopping Condition.
Set Total Events = 5,000 (single stains).
Click Sync stopping conditions to apply to all.



C4. Preview and gate setup

Preview each single stain using Preview.
Adjust gates (“A” and “Positive”) as needed.







TipGate and scale consistency




Apply the same “A” gate to all single stains using Sync Scale and Gate.
The “Positive” gate should be tight and placed on the highest-intensity events.









WarningOff-scale events and voltage changes



If a conjugate is off-scale, reducing PMT voltage can be used to complete acquisition, but the preferred long-term fix is to reduce antibody concentration in future experiments.



Click Stop to move to the next sample.

If it does not advance: right-click tube position -> Set Current Position.




C5. Record single stains

Right-click the first tube (usually “Unstained”) -> Set Current Position.
Acquire single stains:

Manual: Acquire
Automated: Auto Acquire (requires Auto acquisition targets)




C6. Unmixing

Go to Unmixing tab.
Click Unmixing Settings.
If you added an unstained ArC bead control as the negative gate for the live/dead single stain, confirm the negative reference is correctly assigned.
Click Calculate.







NoteSaturation warnings during unmixing



If prompted that saturation of x% is observed: - Small % (e.g., <0.1%): Continue - Large %: the single stain is too bright - Re-run single stain with reduced voltage (Instrument Settings -> Detector & Threshold -> PMT Voltage (%) -> Synchronous Voltage Adjustment) - Preferably: plan to reduce antibody concentration in future experiments



When prompted to apply spectral references to other sample groups with the same laser settings, click Apply.
Confirm the Unmixing toggle (top right) is ON (blue).

title: Sony Spectral Cell Analyzer ID7000
text:
D. Acquire samples

If single stains were already acquired and you are switching racks/plates:

Click Unload and wait for “Plate Unloaded”
Open door, remove rack/plate, close door

Place your sample tubes in the rack according to your Layout Editor assignments.
Open door, load rack onto AutoSampler, close door, click Load.
Confirm Unmixing toggle is ON (blue).
Set/confirm instrument settings (adjust as needed):

Detector & Threshold: FSC Gain and SSC Voltage appropriate for sample
Flow Control:

Sample Flow Rate = 3.0 for previewing ~5 x 10^5 cells in 100 µL
Sample Flow Rate = 8.0 for recording ~5 x 10^5 cells in 100 µL

Agitation: enable, pattern Cyclic, mode Normal
Event Check: On

Set stopping condition (events or time) according to your experimental requirements.
Draw/confirm gating strategy in the worksheet area.
Select the sample to run first: right-click -> Set Current Position.
Click Preview (green arrow) to verify signals are on scale.
Click Record (red circle) to record selected sample, or Auto Acquire to run all auto targets.







WarningAvoid running samples dry



If you need time to adjust axes or gates, stop acquisition to prevent samples running dry.

title: Sony Spectral Cell Analyzer ID7000
text:
E. Export and transfer data






WarningNo external drives



Do not plug external devices (e.g., USB drives) into FCCF computers. Transfer data via approved methods (e.g., BTC cloud), per facility policy.



Under the Experiment pane, click the experiment name (top item in hierarchy).
Right-click -> Export to FCS file.
Export settings:

Under “Pulse Type (for fluorescence)”: uncheck Height and Width
Ensure FCS version = 3.1
Set export location under Save in

Click Export and wait for export progress to complete.
Confirm export has started/completed via the popup and/or log file in output folder.
Transfer exported files to your BTC cloud account (or other approved location).

title: Sony Spectral Cell Analyzer ID7000
text:
F. Cleaning and shutdown

F1. If another user is booked after you

Click Unload.
Remove rack/plate from AutoSampler.
Go to Cytometer tab -> Decontamination.
Select Bleach Cleaning and Rinse and follow prompts to completion.
Remove samples, return tube rack to FCCF fridge.
Close ID7000 software.
Ensure:

Waste tank is empty
Sheath tank is full for next user








NoteRed error light after closing software



After the software closes, a red “Error” light on the ID7000 is normal and indicates the instrument is not connected to the computer.




F2. If you are the last user for the day

Click Unload.
Remove rack/plate from AutoSampler.
Go to Cytometer tab -> Hardware Shutdown.
Select Bleach Cleaning and Rinse and follow prompts to complete decontamination and shutdown.
Remove samples, return tube rack to FCCF fridge.
After shutdown completes and cytometer switches off automatically, close the software.
Ensure waste is empty and sheath is full for next user.

title: 37% Percoll Solution (= 33% final Percoll)
text:
Definitions

V_T = total final volume

V_P = volume of Percoll (contains no salts)

V_10x = volume of 10x PBS

The remaining volume is 1x PBS.

title: 37% Percoll Solution (= 33% final Percoll)
text:
Salt balance logic
The final solution must contain the same total amount of salt as V_T mL of 1x PBS.
Salt contributions: - Percoll contributes 0x - 1x PBS contributes 1x - 10x PBS contributes 10x

Step 1: Express total salt content
(V_T - V_P - V_10x) + 10 · V_10x = V_T


Step 2: Combine terms
V_T - V_P + 9 · V_10x = V_T


Step 3: Subtract V_T from both sides
- V_P + 9 · V_10x = 0


Step 4: Rearrange
9 · V_10x = V_P


Final rule
V_10x = V_P / 9
In words:
For every 9 mL of Percoll, add 1 mL of 10x PBS to make the solution isotonic.

title: ARCHIVAL Isolation of Liver-Associated Lymphocytes (LALs) Including NLCs from Mouse Liver
text:
Step 1 – Preparation and setup

Pre-cool solutions

Pre-cool PBS on ice for liver perfusion and transport.

Label collection vessels (choose one option per experiment)

Option A: 6-well plate collection

Label one well per mouse in a 6-well plate.
Add ~3–5 mL ice-cold PBS per well.

Option B: 50 mL tube collection

Label one 50 mL conical tube per liver.
Add 5 mL ice-cold PBS per tube.


Label dissociation and processing tubes

Label gentleMACS C-tubes (or equivalent) for each liver.
Label additional 50 mL tubes as required for downstream steps.

Prepare buffers (see separate buffer protocols)

Liver digestion buffer (BUF-MUS-LIV-DIG-001; collagenase IV + DNase I in PBS).
37% Percoll working solution (BUF-GEN-PERC-37PCT-001).
ACK lysis buffer (BUF-GEN-ACK-LYSIS-001).
FACS buffer (BUF-GEN-FACS-BUF-001), if required for downstream applications.

Warm digestion components

Turn on a water bath and set to 37 °C.
Place an aliquot of liver digestion buffer in the water bath to pre-warm.
If digestion buffer will be prepared later, pre-warm DMEM or PBS instead.

Equipment setup

Set a refrigerated benchtop centrifuge to 4 °C.
Ensure access to a gentleMACS instrument with an appropriate liver dissociation program.

Items to take to the animal facility

Ice bucket with ice-cold PBS.
6-well plates and/or pre-filled 50 mL tubes (as chosen above).
Sterile scissors and forceps.
10 mL syringes (one per mouse or per treatment group).
Needles for liver perfusion (recommended 25G or 26G).
Absorbent pads and waste container for perfusion runoff.

title: ARCHIVAL Isolation of Liver-Associated Lymphocytes (LALs) Including NLCs from Mouse Liver
section: Step 2 – Mouse sacrifice and liver perfusion
text:
Step 2 – Mouse sacrifice and liver perfusion

Sacrifice mice according to institutional and ethical guidelines (e.g. CO₂ asphyxiation followed by cervical dislocation, as approved).
Place the mouse in a supine position on a suitable surface.
Open the abdominal cavity to expose the liver and major vessels.
Perfuse the liver with ice-cold PBS via one of the following routes:

Inferior vena cava

Portal vein

Directly via the heart

Gently insert a needle into the chosen vessel and perfuse with PBS until the liver visibly blanches (typically ~5–10 mL per mouse).







Note



Efficient perfusion reduces blood content and improves the quality of density separation and downstream staining.



After perfusion, proceed immediately to liver collection.

title: ARCHIVAL Isolation of Liver-Associated Lymphocytes (LALs) Including NLCs from Mouse Liver
text:
Step 3 – Liver collection and mincing

Excise the perfused liver using sterile, autoclaved instruments.
Transfer the liver to the pre-labelled 50 mL conical tube or to the appropriate well of a 6-well plate containing ice-cold PBS.
Keep the tube or plate on ice at all times.
(Optional but highly recommended) Weigh the liver

Briefly place the liver on blotting paper to wick off excess liquid.
Weigh the liver and record the weight in the lab book.

Add 4 mL of pre-warmed liver digestion buffer to a labelled gentleMACS C-tube (one tube per liver).
Transfer the liver into the gentleMACS C-tube containing digestion buffer.
Using sterile curved scissors, mince the liver directly within the gentleMACS C-tube until tissue fragments are approximately ~2–3 mm.
Secure the C-tube onto the gentleMACS instrument.







Note



Ensure all tissue pieces are fully submerged in digestion buffer and not stuck to the walls or base of the tube.



Place the warming sleeve over the tube.
Run program HH17 (17-minute digestion).







Warning



After starting the run, confirm that all tubes are correctly seated and rotating properly.
If a tube is not spinning, stop the run, remove the tube, reseat it, and restart the program.








Important



Do not leave livers in digestion buffer for prolonged periods. Over-digestion can strip surface epitopes and negatively impact downstream staining and phenotyping.
Note: the gentleMACS instrument does not beep when the program finishes—set a timer or alarm before starting the run.








Warning



Make sure the gentleMACS C-tube is firmly closed and correctly positioned. Leaks during the run can lead to sample loss and contamination of the instrument.

title: ARCHIVAL Isolation of Liver-Associated Lymphocytes (LALs) Including NLCs from Mouse Liver
section: Step 5 – Removal of hepatocytes and washing
text:
Step 5 – Removal of hepatocytes and washing

After digestion, transfer the liver cell suspension from the C-tube into a 50 mL conical tube.
Rinse the C-tube with ice-cold PBS and add the rinse to the same 50 mL tube to maximize yield.
Bring the volume up to 50 mL with ice-cold PBS.
Centrifuge at 50 g for 2 min at 4 °C to sediment hepatocytes.
Carefully transfer the supernatant (containing lymphocytes and smaller cells) to a fresh 50 mL tube without disturbing the hepatocyte pellet.
Adjust the volume to 50 mL with ice-cold PBS.
Centrifuge at 550 g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and keep the cell pellet on ice.

title: ARCHIVAL Isolation of Liver-Associated Lymphocytes (LALs) Including NLCs from Mouse Liver
section: Step 6 – 37 % Percoll enrichment of liver-associated lymphocytes
text:
Step 6 – 37 % Percoll enrichment of liver-associated lymphocytes

While the liver samples are pelleting, aliquot 10 mL of 37% Percoll (BUF-GEN-PERC-37PCT-001, prepared in PBS) into labelled 15 mL conical tubes (one tube per liver).
Carefully aspirate the supernatant from the liver cell pellet in the 50 mL tube.
Using a transfer pipette, 1 mL pipette, or serological pipette, take up approximately 1 mL of 37% Percoll from the corresponding 15 mL tube and use it to gently resuspend the liver cell pellet in the 50 mL tube.
Transfer the resuspended cells back into the labelled 15 mL Percoll tube.
Repeat the rinse once or twice with additional small volumes of Percoll, if needed, to ensure all remaining liver cells are recovered from the 50 mL tube.
Cap the 15 mL tube and invert gently 2–3 times to ensure complete mixing.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 20 min at room temperature (RT; ~20–22 °C) using:

Moderate acceleration (e.g. acc 7)
Minimal brake (e.g. br 1) to avoid disturbing the gradient








Important



Do not leave liver samples in Percoll for longer than necessary. Prolonged exposure can reduce cell viability and negatively impact downstream applications. Plan spins and downstream steps in advance.








Warning



Avoid high brake settings during Percoll centrifugation. Abrupt braking can disrupt the gradient and reduce lymphocyte enrichment.



After centrifugation, carefully asiprate the supernatant.
Resuspend the enriched lymphocyte pellet in 20–30 mL ice-cold PBS.
Centrifuge at 550 g) for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and keep the pellet on ice.

title: ARCHIVAL Isolation of Liver-Associated Lymphocytes (LALs) Including NLCs from Mouse Liver
text:
STEP 7 – RBC lysis and filtration

Add 1 mL RBC lysis buffer per liver to the cell pellet:

HybriMax RBC Lysis Buffer: incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature, or

ACK lysis buffer: incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.


Gently resuspend the pellet by pipetting or flicking immediately after adding buffer.

After incubation, quench the lysis by topping up to 50 mL with FACS Buffer.







Warning



Do not exceed the indicated incubation times. Over-lysis (particularly >5 minutes with HybriMax or >2 minutes with ACK) can reduce leukocyte viability.



Pass the suspension through a 70 µm cell strainer into a fresh 50 mL tube kept on ice.
Rinse the strainer with an additional 5–10 mL PBS if needed to recover remaining cells.
Centrifuge at 550 g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and keep the pellet on ice.

title: ARCHIVAL Isolation of Liver-Associated Lymphocytes (LALs) Including NLCs from Mouse Liver
text:
Step 8 – Final wash and resuspension

Resuspend the cell pellet in 10 mL ice-cold PBS.
Count cells and assess viability (e.g. trypan blue) as required.
Proceed with downstream applications (e.g. flow cytometry, sorting, or culture of NLCs).

text:
A. Prepare “Liver Digestion Buffer (no DNase)”
This buffer is DMEM + Collagenase D, without DNase. It is frozen in aliquots for convenient use.






Note



Collagenase and DNase I are proteins and mechanically sensitive. Avoid vigorous vortexing or shaking, as this can denature the enzymes and reduce activity. Mix by gentle inversion or slow pipetting to preserve enzymatic function.



Thaw a Collagenase D 100 mg/mL stock aliquot on ice or at 4 °C.
In a sterile tube, prepare the digestion stock for the desired number of aliquots, for example:

For each 5 mL stock aliquot:

Add 5 mL DMEM (incomplete).
Add 50 µL Collagenase D stock (100 mg/mL).
Mix gently by inversion (avoid foaming).


Aliquot the digestion buffer into sterile tubes (e.g. 5–10 mL per aliquot, depending on typical experimental usage, note: 5 mL per liver).
Label aliquots clearly with:

“Liver Digestion Buffer (no DNase)”
Date
Initials

Freeze aliquots at −20 °C.

title: Mouse Liver Digestion Buffer with Collagenase D
section: B. Prepare final working Liver Digestion Buffer (day of use)
text:
B. Prepare final working Liver Digestion Buffer (day of use)

Remove the required number of Liver Digestion Buffer (no DNase) aliquots from −20 °C and thaw at room temperature or 4 °C.
For each 5 mL of final working buffer needed:

Ensure the thawed buffer is well mixed (gentle inversion).
Add 5 µL DNase I stock (10 mg/mL) to 5 mL digestion buffer
Mix gently by inversion.

Pre-warm the final working buffer to 37 °C before use (e.g. water bath or incubator).
If desired, pre-aliquot 5 mL of the final working buffer into pre-labelled 50 mL tubes for liver digestion.







Tip



To minimise variability, prepare all working-buffer aliquots for a given experiment at the same time using the same DNase stock, and keep buffers at 37 °C only for as long as required during digestion.








Note



DNase I is added only on the day of use because prolonged storage in digestion buffer containing active collagenase can lead to proteolytic degradation of DNase.

title: CellTrace Violet (CTV) Staining of Lymphocytes
text:
Step 1 – Cell preparation and resting

If using frozen PBMCs:

Thaw vials rapidly in a 37 °C water bath until a small ice crystal remains.
Immediately transfer the cell suspension into a tube containing pre-warmed R10 medium (BUF-R10-MED) and mix gently.
Centrifuge at ~400–500 g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in fresh R10.

Optionally add DNase I (e.g. 10 µL/mL of an appropriate stock) to reduce clumping during the initial rest period.
Incubate cells at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for ~1 hour to recover from thawing and improve viability.
Count cells and assess viability using trypan blue or an equivalent method.
Adjust the cell concentration as needed to allow resuspension at 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL in PBS in the next step.

title: CellTrace Violet (CTV) Staining of Lymphocytes
section: Step 2 – Preparation of CellTrace Violet stock
text:
Step 2 – Preparation of CellTrace Violet stock

Reconstitute one vial of CellTrace Violet in 20 µL DMSO in a biosafety cabinet.
Mix gently by pipetting; avoid foaming or vortexing.
Aliquot the stock if desired and store according to the manufacturer’s recommendations (typically −20 °C, protected from light).







Note



Prepare CTV stock fresh on the day of use or use single-use aliquots to avoid repeated freeze–thaw cycles.

title: CellTrace Violet (CTV) Staining of Lymphocytes
text:
Step 3 – CTV staining

Pellet cells and resuspend in PBS without FCS at 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL.
For each mL of cell suspension, add 0.2–0.5 µL of the CTV stock solution (based on prior titration).
Immediately mix by gentle pipetting or brief low-speed vortexing to ensure even distribution of the dye.
Incubate cells for 20 min at room temperature, protected from light.
During incubation, gently invert or tap the tube once or twice to maintain a uniform suspension.







Warning



Do not stain cells in R10 or other serum-containing media. Proteins in the medium will quench the dye and lead to weak or inconsistent staining.

title: CellTrace Violet (CTV) Staining of Lymphocytes
text:
Step 4 – Quenching and washing

After 20 min, add 5× the original staining volume of pre-warmed R10 (e.g. add 5 mL R10 to 1 mL stained cells) to quench unbound dye.
Incubate for 5 min at room temperature, protected from light.
Centrifuge at ~400–500 g for 5 min (or ~1200 rpm in a standard cell-culture centrifuge, if this corresponds to the correct g-force).
Discard the supernatant carefully.
Optional extended wash (recommended for higher CTV concentrations or sensitive cell types):

Resuspend cells in up to 10 mL R10.

Centrifuge again at ~400–500 g for 5 min.

Discard the supernatant.

Repeat once more if residual dye is a concern.

title: CellTrace Violet (CTV) Staining of Lymphocytes
text:
Step 5 – Final resuspension and equilibration

Resuspend cells in R10 (BUF-R10-MED) at the desired concentration for stimulation or culture (commonly 0.5–2 × 10⁶ cells/mL).
Incubate for at least 10 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to allow stabilization of dye distribution within the cells.
Proceed with downstream steps such as:

Addition of stimuli for proliferation assays.
Plating for co-culture experiments.
Subsequent staining for surface markers prior to acquisition.

title: 4D-Nucleofector CRISPR–Cas9 RNP Delivery to T and NK Cells
section: Step 2 – gRNA duplex and RNP preparation
text:
Step 2 – gRNA duplex and RNP preparation
This section assumes use of crRNA + tracrRNA duplexes and recombinant Cas9 protein.

2.1 crRNA:tracrRNA duplexing

Thaw crRNA and tracrRNA aliquots on ice.

Mix crRNA and tracrRNA at equimolar concentrations (e.g. each at 100 µM) to generate a duplex:

Example: 5 µL crRNA (100 µM) + 5 µL tracrRNA (100 µM) → 10 µL duplex at 100 µM.

Incubate at 95 °C for 5 min, then allow to cool to room temperature (bench-top) for at least 10 min, or follow vendor instructions.
Store duplexed gRNA on ice during RNP preparation.



2.2 RNP assembly

Thaw Cas9 protein aliquots on ice.

For each nucleofection reaction, prepare RNP mix in a low-bind tube:

Example per reaction (starting point, adjust using Table 1):

1.5 µL gRNA duplex (100 µM) → 150 pmol gRNA

3.0 µL Cas9 (20 µM) → 60 pmol Cas9

Optional: add nuclease-free water to increase handling volume, if needed.


Gently mix by pipetting; avoid bubbles.

Incubate the RNP mix at 37 °C for 15 min.

After incubation, keep RNP at room temperature or on ice and use within 1–2 hours for nucleofection.







Warning



Do not repeatedly freeze–thaw Cas9 or gRNA aliquots. Prepare small working aliquots and discard thawed leftovers at the end of the day to preserve activity.

title: 4D-Nucleofector CRISPR–Cas9 RNP Delivery to T and NK Cells
text:
Step 3 – Cell preparation
The steps below describe the unified handling for all T and NK cell types. Follow cell-type–specific culture SOPs for prior expansion and activation.

3.1 Harvesting cells

Harvest cells from culture flasks or plates at the desired time point (e.g. 2–3 days post activation for T cells; 3 days post priming for NK).

For suspension cultures (mouse NK, NK-92, activated T cells): gently resuspend by pipetting up and down.

For mixed cultures (e.g. mouse spleen-derived T or NK), process according to the relevant isolation SOP (e.g. magnetic separation) before nucleofection.



3.2 Washing and counting

Transfer cells to 15 mL conical tubes.

Centrifuge at 300–400 g for 5 min at room temperature.

Carefully aspirate supernatant.

Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL DPBS or PBS and mix gently.

Centrifuge again under the same conditions.

Aspirate the supernatant completely.

Take an aliquot and count cells (e.g. trypan blue exclusion).

Calculate total cell number and plan 0.5–1.0 × 10⁶ cells per nucleofection reaction.







Warning



Residual serum or culture medium in the pellet will reduce nucleofection efficiency and viability. After the final wash, remove supernatant carefully and completely before adding nucleofector solution.

title: 4D-Nucleofector CRISPR–Cas9 RNP Delivery to T and NK Cells
section: Step 4 – Resuspension in nucleofector solution and mixing with RNP
text:
Step 4 – Resuspension in nucleofector solution and mixing with RNP

4.1 Preparation of nucleofector cell suspension

Pre-equilibrate nucleofector solutions (P3, P4, SE) to room temperature as recommended by the manufacturer.

For each cell type, prepare enough nucleofector solution for all planned reactions, following the kit instructions (e.g. supplementing solution with additive as required).

Resuspend washed cells in the appropriate nucleofector solution at a concentration of:

5 × 10⁷ cells/mL for 1.0 × 10⁶ cells in 20 µL

2.5 × 10⁷ cells/mL for 0.5 × 10⁶ cells in 20 µL

Gently mix and keep at room temperature. Avoid leaving cells in nucleofector solution for longer than 15–20 min before pulsing.



4.2 Mixing cells with RNP
For each reaction:

Aliquot the appropriate volume of RNP mix into a fresh low-bind tube or directly into the well/strip position (e.g. 4.5 µL per reaction).

Add nucleofector cell suspension to reach a total volume of 20 µL per reaction:

Example: 4.5 µL RNP + 15.5 µL cell suspension.


Gently pipette up and down to mix; avoid introducing air bubbles.

Immediately proceed to loading the Nucleocuvette™.

title: 4D-Nucleofector CRISPR–Cas9 RNP Delivery to T and NK Cells
section: Step 5 – Loading Nucleocuvette™ and running the 4D program
text:
Step 5 – Loading Nucleocuvette™ and running the 4D program

5.1 Loading Nucleocuvette™ strips

Place the 20 µL Nucleocuvette™ strip into its holder.

Carefully pipette 20 µL of the RNP–cell mix into each well, aiming the pipette tip to the side of the well to minimise bubbles.

Visually inspect each well for uniform filling and absence of air pockets.

Insert the holder into the 4D-Nucleofector X unit.



5.2 Selecting and running programs

On the 4D-Nucleofector control unit, select the nucleofection program corresponding to the cell type (see lookup table in Step 1).

Confirm that the selected program and kit (P3, P4, SE) match the cells in the strip.

Start the nucleofection run.

When complete, remove the Nucleocuvette™ strip promptly and place it in a biosafety cabinet.







Note



If running multiple cell types in parallel, clearly separate strips by cell type and program to avoid mismatches. Only one program can be used per strip/run.

title: 4D-Nucleofector CRISPR–Cas9 RNP Delivery to T and NK Cells
text:
Step 6 – Immediate post-nucleofection rescue

6.1 Addition of rescue medium in cuvette

Immediately after nucleofection, add 60–100 µL of pre-warmed culture medium directly into each Nucleocuvette™ well:

Use the appropriate base medium (e.g. T-cell medium, NK medium, or NK-92 medium).

Cytokines may be omitted from this initial rescue step if preferred (see cell-type notes below).

Gently pipette up and down once to mix, without generating bubbles.

Place the Nucleocuvette™ strip into a 37 °C incubator (inside a sterile container) or keep at 37 °C in the biosafety cabinet if feasible.
Allow cells to recover in the cuvette for 10–25 min.



6.2 Transfer to culture plates

After the recovery period, gently resuspend each Nucleocuvette™ well by pipetting up and down.

Transfer the entire volume (typically 80–120 µL) into the corresponding well of a pre-warmed 96- or 48-well plate or into a culture tube containing:

Final volume: 200–1000 µL per well/tube.

Appropriate cytokine supplementation, for example:

Naïve mouse T: IL-7 ± low IL-2.

Activated T (mouse/human): IL-2 ± IL-7.

Mouse NK: IL-15 + IL-2 as per NK culture SOP.

NK-92: NK-92 medium ± IL-2 as per NK-92 culture SOP.


Adjust final cell density to 0.5–1.0 × 10⁶ cells/mL for standard culture.

Incubate plates at 37 °C, 5% CO₂.







Warning



Do not leave nucleofected cells in undiluted nucleofector buffer longer than necessary. Rescue medium should be added within minutes after the pulse and cells should be transferred to standard culture conditions within 30–40 min.

title: 4D-Nucleofector CRISPR–Cas9 RNP Delivery to T and NK Cells
text:
Step 7 – Recommended timelines for analysis
Although the exact timepoint will depend on the target locus and downstream readouts, the following windows are commonly used:

Mouse NK cells: assess viability and KO efficiency at day 3 and day 7.

Mouse T cells (naïve/activated): assess between day 3–6, with extended phenotyping up to day 10–15 when needed.

Human T cells (activated): assess at day 3–5 post nucleofection.

NK-92: assess between day 3–5 post nucleofection.

Choice of timepoint should balance maximal editing efficiency with sufficient recovery and expansion.

Step 2 – Thawing K-562 cells

Pre-warm 10–15 mL of complete medium to 37 °C.
Thaw a cryovial of K-562 cells in a 37 °C water bath:

Gently swirl and remove when only a small ice crystal remains.

title: K-562 Cell Line Culture Protocol
text:
Step 3 – Routine culture and passaging

Recommended density

Maintain between 2 × 10⁵ and 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL.



Procedure

Gently resuspend the culture by pipetting up and down.
Count cells using trypan blue or an automated counter.
If density > 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL:

Split culture 1:2 to 1:5 depending on growth.

Add fresh, pre-warmed complete medium to adjust culture to:

2–3 × 10⁵ cells/mL

Return to incubator (37 °C, 5% CO₂).







Warning



Do not allow cultures to sit for more than 3–4 days without splitting. Nutrient depletion leads to apoptosis and growth arrest.

title: K-562 Cell Line Culture Protocol

Step 4 – Short-term storage / holding conditions

Cultures may be held at 2–4 × 10⁵ cells/mL for 24–48 h without splitting.
If cultures appear slow or viability drops:

Increase medium volume

Spin down and resuspend in entirely fresh medium

90% FCS + 10% DMSO
(or use BUF-FREEZE-MIX diluted 1:1 with cell suspension)

Collect cells in exponential growth phase.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min.
Resuspend in freezing medium at 1–10 × 10⁶ cells/mL.
Aliquot 1 mL into labelled cryovials.
Place vials into a controlled-rate freezing container (e.g. Mr Frosty).
Freeze at −70/−80 °C overnight.
Transfer vials to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage.

title: Mouse Bone Marrow Isolation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 1 – Bone collection

Euthanise the mouse using an approved method.
Spray the hind limbs with 70% ethanol and transfer the carcass to a sterile working area (e.g. Class II biosafety cabinet, if available).
Dissect out femurs using scissors and forceps.
Remove all excess muscle and connective tissue from the bones.
Place cleaned bones in a 50 mL tube or petri dish containing cold FACS Buffer or PBS and keep on ice.







Tip



Note how many bones per mice for later cell number calculations

title: Mouse Bone Marrow Isolation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 2 – Bone marrow extraction

Method 1 - Flushing the bone marrow

In a petri dish or on a sterile surface, cut off the epiphyses (ends) of each bone with sterile scissors to expose the marrow cavity.
Fill a 10 mL syringe fitted with an appropriate gauge needle (e.g. 25 G) with cold FACS Buffer or PBS.
Position the needle into one end of the bone and flush the marrow into a petri dish or 50 mL tube:

Use ~1–3 mL buffer per bone, depending on size.

Repeat flushing from both ends if necessary until the bone appears pale and empty.
Gently triturate the flushed marrow with a 5–10 mL pipette or by drawing up and down with the syringe (without needle) to break up clumps.







Warning



Avoid vigorous pipetting that shears cells; use gentle, repeated strokes to obtain a single-cell suspension.




Method 2 - Centrifugation

Poke a small hole (using a needle) in a PCR tube
Place PCR tube in an Eppendorf tube
Add 200 µL cold FACS Buffer
Cut off the epiphyses (ends) of each bone with sterile scissors to expose the marrow cavity.
Spin in table-top micro-centrifuge for 30 sec - 2 mins
Ensure bone marrow has not gotten stuck in the PCR tube and bones appear pale and empty (Repeat spin as needed)

title: Mouse Bone Marrow Isolation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 3 – Filtration and initial wash

Pass sample through a 70 µm cell strainer onto a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Rinse the petri dish/source tube and strainer with additional cold FACS Buffer to collect remaining cells and top up to 15 mL.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Carefully discard the supernatant.

title: Mouse Bone Marrow Isolation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 4 – RBC lysis (if required)

Gently resuspend the bone marrow pellet in 100 µL 1× RBC Lysis Buffer (e.g. HybriMax or equivalent).
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature, gently inverting the tube once or twice.







Warning



Do not exceed 5 minutes of RBC lysis; prolonged exposure can reduce leukocyte viability and alter surface marker expression.



After lysis, immediately top up the tube to 10 mL with FACS Buffer.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Carefully discard the supernatant.

title: Mouse Bone Marrow Isolation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 5 – Final wash and resuspension

Resuspend cells in 1 mL FACS Buffer (adjust volume according to desired final concentration and downstream application).
Gently flick or briefly vortex to loosen the pellet.
If residual clumping is observed, pass the suspension again through a 70 µm strainer into a fresh tube.
Keep the suspension on ice until counting, staining, or further processing.

title: Mouse Bone Marrow Isolation to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 6 – Downstream applications
Proceed to:

Cell counting and viability assessment.
Flow cytometry staining panels (e.g. hematopoietic profiling).
FACS sorting (e.g. HSCs, progenitors, mature lineages).
Functional assays or in vitro culture as per experimental design.

text:
Overview of the intestinal tract
The mouse intestinal tract runs approximately 30 cm in total and is divided into the small intestine and large intestine, each with distinct anatomy, function, and immune composition.

Small intestine
The small intestine comprises three contiguous segments, running proximal to distal:









Segment
Approximate proportion
Key anatomical features
Primary function




Duodenum
~5% of SI length
Short; receives bile and pancreatic secretions; long villi (villus:crypt ~3–5:1)
Digestion of fats, carbohydrates, protein; iron absorption


Jejunum
~40% of SI length
Longest segment; most active absorption; longest and densest villi
Primary nutrient absorption


Ileum
~55% of SI length
Shorter villi; highest density of Peyer’s patches; terminal segment before cecum
Vitamin B12 and bile acid reabsorption; immune sampling



The small intestinal epithelium is organised into finger-like villi projecting into the lumen (absent in the large intestine) and crypts of Lieberkühn at the base of the villi. This villus–crypt architecture dramatically increases luminal surface area and is the structural context within which IELs reside.


Large intestine
The large intestine follows the small intestine and comprises:







Segment
Notes




Cecum
Blind-ended pouch at the SI–LI junction; largest microbial reservoir; enlarged in germ-free mice


Colon (proximal → distal)
Lacks villi; has crypts only; much thicker mucus layer than SI; primary site of water reabsorption


Rectum / anus
Terminal segment



The large intestine has a far higher microbial load than the small intestine (bacterial density increases ~1,000-fold from duodenum to colon) and a correspondingly distinct immune environment dominated by regulatory and microbiota-responsive cells.






Note



IEL density is substantially higher in the small intestine than the large intestine. The large intestine has approximately 5–10× fewer IELs per epithelial cell than the small intestine under steady-state conditions. This protocol targets small intestinal IELs only.

title: Mouse Small Intestinal Intraepithelial Lymphocyte (IEL) Isolation
text:
Wall architecture and immune compartments
The intestinal wall is organised into concentric layers. Moving from the lumen outward:
Lumen
  │
  ▼
Epithelium          ← IELs live here (within the epithelial layer)
  │
Basement membrane
  │
Lamina propria      ← LPLs, DCs, macrophages, mast cells, ILCs
  │
Muscularis mucosae
  │
Submucosa           ← Nerve plexus, blood and lymphatic vessels
  │
Muscularis externa  ← Smooth muscle (inner circular + outer longitudinal)
  │
Serosa / mesentery
For immunological purposes, the two most important layers are the epithelium and the lamina propria.

Epithelial layer and the IEL compartment
The intestinal epithelium is a single-cell-thick monolayer of epithelial cells (primarily enterocytes) that lines the entire luminal surface. IELs are embedded within this monolayer, sitting between neighbouring epithelial cells with their cell bodies typically below the tight junctions but above the basement membrane. They are in direct contact with the epithelium and sample the luminal environment.
In the small intestine, there is approximately 1 IEL per 5–10 epithelial cells, making the gut epithelium one of the largest T cell compartments in the body by cell number. IELs are long-lived, largely non-recirculating tissue-resident cells.
How to access IELs: Because IELs are mechanically held within the epithelial layer by integrin interactions (primarily αEβ7/CD103), they are released by disrupting epithelial junctions with EDTA (chelates calcium, destabilising E-cadherin-based junctions) and DTT (reduces disulfide bonds in mucus), combined with mechanical agitation. This is the stripping step in this protocol.


Lamina propria and the LPL compartment
The lamina propria is the loose connective tissue layer immediately beneath the epithelium, separated from it by the basement membrane. It contains:

T cells — predominantly CD4+ T helper cells; also CD8+ effector T cells; Tregs
B cells and plasma cells — IgA-secreting plasma cells are abundant; responsible for secretory IgA production
Dendritic cells — CD11b+CD8α− DCs predominate in the small intestinal LP; important for antigen sampling and T cell priming
Macrophages — major phagocytic and tolerogenic population; form close contacts with the epithelium
Mast cells — involved in helminth responses and barrier defence
Innate lymphoid cells (ILCs) — ILC1, ILC2, ILC3 populations present; ILC3s produce IL-22 for barrier maintenance

How to access LPLs: The basement membrane must be disrupted after removing the epithelial layer. This requires enzymatic digestion of the remaining tissue with collagenase (± DNase), typically at 37 °C with agitation. LPL isolation is a separate workflow from IEL isolation and is not covered in this protocol. The intestinal pieces remaining after the stripping and shake steps in this protocol can be used directly as input for LP digestion.


Peyer’s patches
Peyer’s patches are organised lymphoid follicles embedded in the intestinal wall, predominantly in the ileum. They are visible as pale, dome-shaped nodules on the anti-mesenteric surface. They contain:

Dense B cell follicles (B220+ B cells)
Germinal centre reactions for IgA class switching
T cell zones with CD4+ T cells
Specialised M cells (microfold cells) in the overlying follicle-associated epithelium for antigen transcytosis

Peyer’s patches are not part of the IEL or LP compartments and must be removed before processing. If retained, the B cell-rich follicular content heavily contaminates IEL preparations and distorts flow cytometry data.

IEL subset distribution is not uniform along the small intestine. The two major functional categories of IELs are:

Natural IELs (nIELs) — arise from thymic precursors; present in germ-free mice; include TCRγδ+ IELs and TCRαβ+ CD8αα+ IELs. More abundant in the proximal SI (duodenum/jejunum).

Microbiota-dependent immune cell shaping — colonic immune cell composition is more severely disrupted in germ-free conditions than SI.
Fewer IELs and DCs — under homeostatic conditions; both are recruited upon inflammation.
No villi — crypts only; different epithelial cell organisation affects IEL numbers and accessibility.

title: Mouse Small Intestinal Intraepithelial Lymphocyte (IEL) Isolation
text:
STEP 1 – Preparation and setup

Prepare all buffers fresh (see Buffers section). Pre-warm Strip Medium to 37 °C in a water bath. Keep all other buffers on ice.
Set up a magnetic stir plate at 37 °C with a stir bar and a beaker — this is used for the stripping step.
Prepare a metal strainer over a large collection beaker for filtering after stripping.
Label 50 mL tubes for each mouse: one for stripping collection, one for downstream processing.
Pre-cool the centrifuge to 4 °C.
Prepare 35% Percoll working solution (see Buffers section) at room temperature.

title: Mouse Small Intestinal Intraepithelial Lymphocyte (IEL) Isolation
text:
STEP 2 – Intestine harvest and preparation

Euthanise the mouse by an approved method.
Open the abdominal cavity and locate the small intestine.
Excise the entire small intestine, cutting just distal to the pyloric sphincter (stomach) and at the ileocecal junction.
Remove all attached mesenteric fat and connective tissue along the intestinal length.
Identify and excise all Peyer’s patches (pale, dome-shaped lymphoid nodules on the anti-mesenteric border). Cut them away and discard.







Warning



Peyer’s patches must be removed completely. They contain a distinct lymphoid population that will contaminate the IEL fraction.



Cut the intestine open longitudinally along its entire length using fine scissors.
Wash the opened intestine once with 3% Medium and then once with PBS to remove luminal contents and mucus.
After washing, transfer the intestinal tissue to a 50 mL Falcon tube with a small volume of 3% Medium to keep it moist until the next step.







Note



Thorough washing after opening is critical. Residual mucus reduces stripping efficiency.

title: Mouse Small Intestinal Intraepithelial Lymphocyte (IEL) Isolation
text:
STEP 3 – DTT/EDTA stripping (37 °C magnetic stir)

Cut the washed intestinal tissue into approximately 5 pieces of roughly equal length.
Place the pieces into the pre-warmed beaker (on the magnetic stir plate at 37 °C) containing 20 mL Strip Medium (RPMI/3% FCS + 1 mM DTT + 5 mM EDTA, pre-warmed to 37 °C).
Add a magnetic stir bar to the beaker. Cover with aluminium foil.
Incubate at 37 °C for 20 minutes with continuous stirring at 250 rpm.







Warning



Do not exceed the 20-minute incubation or increase DTT concentration above 1 mM. Over-exposure to DTT reduces leukocyte viability.



After incubation, strain the contents through the metal strainer into the collection beaker to collect the stripped epithelial fraction.
Keep the intestinal pieces on the strainer for the manual shake step (STEP 4).

title: Mouse Small Intestinal Intraepithelial Lymphocyte (IEL) Isolation
text:
STEP 4 – Manual shake washes
The mechanical shake step dislodges residual IELs from the tissue and maximises recovery.

Shake round 1

Transfer the intestinal pieces from the metal strainer into a 50 mL Falcon tube containing 10 mL Shake Medium (RPMI + 1% glutamine + 1% Pen/Strep + 2% HEPES + 2 mM EDTA).
Cap the tube and shake vigorously by hand for 30 seconds.
Pour the tube contents back through the metal strainer into the collection beaker.



Shake round 2

Return the intestinal pieces to the Falcon tube with a fresh 10 mL Shake Medium.
Shake vigorously for 30 seconds as before.
Pour back through the metal strainer into the collection beaker.

The collection beaker now contains the pooled stripping and shake fractions. The intestinal tissue pieces can be discarded or retained for LP isolation.

title: Mouse Small Intestinal Intraepithelial Lymphocyte (IEL) Isolation
text:
STEP 5 – Transfer and centrifugation

Transfer the total cell suspension from the collection beaker into a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 400 g, 4 °C, 10 minutes.







Note



The colleague protocol reports 550 g for this step. Standard published IEL protocols use 400 × g for this wash spin. Confirm with your local centrifuge rotor to determine the exact rpm corresponding to your instrument settings.



Discard the supernatant.

title: Mouse Small Intestinal Intraepithelial Lymphocyte (IEL) Isolation
text:
STEP 6 – 35% Percoll enrichment

Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of 35% Percoll.







Note



On Percoll percentage: This protocol uses 35% Percoll as per the collaborator protocol. Literature precedent for mouse IEL isolation varies: single-density pellet-through protocols typically use 35–44%, while discontinuous gradient protocols use 44%/67% (interface collection) for higher purity. The 44/67% discontinuous gradient consistently yields 30–80% CD45+ lymphocytes post-separation and is used in the most widely cited murine IEL protocols (Lefrancois & Lycke 2001; Bhatt & Bhatt 2022 PMC8128104). A 37% single-density pellet-through (the concentration used in the lab for liver) should also work for IEL and is compatible with this workflow; lymphocytes pellet while many epithelial cells and debris remain in the supernatant. If purity is insufficient with 35–37%, consider switching to the 44/67% discontinuous gradient approach.



Centrifuge at 800 g, 25 minutes, room temperature (20–22 °C):

Acceleration: moderate (acc 7)
Brake: minimal (br 1)








Warning



Do not use high brake — abrupt deceleration disrupts the interface and reduces enrichment.



After centrifugation:

Lymphocytes pellet at the bottom.
Epithelial cells, debris, and dead cells remain in the supernatant.

Carefully aspirate and discard the supernatant in one smooth motion.
Wash the pellet: resuspend in PBS, centrifuge at 400 g, 4 °C, 10 minutes. Discard supernatant.

title: Mouse Small Intestinal Intraepithelial Lymphocyte (IEL) Isolation
text:
STEP 7 – ACK RBC lysis (optional)






Note



RBC contamination in IEL preparations is generally low because the intestinal epithelial compartment contains few red blood cells. This step can often be omitted, particularly if a Percoll gradient has been performed. Include if the pellet appears visibly red.



Resuspend the cell pellet in 7 mL ACK lysis buffer.
Incubate for approximately 10 minutes at room temperature.
Pass the suspension through a 70 µm cell strainer into a fresh 50 mL tube.
Top up to 30 mL with PBS.
Centrifuge at 400 g, 4 °C, 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.

title: Mouse Small Intestinal Intraepithelial Lymphocyte (IEL) Isolation
text:
STEP 8 – Final resuspension and staining

Resuspend the cell pellet in 300 µL PBS.
Count cells and assess viability as required.
Use 100 µL of suspension per flow cytometry panel.
Add 100 µL antibody master mix and stain for 20 minutes (on ice, protected from light, as per staining SOP).
After staining, resuspend in 200 µL PBS for acquisition.







Tip



Expected yield from one small intestine: approximately 3–6 × 10^6 total IEL from an 8–12-week-old naïve C57BL/6 mouse after Percoll enrichment (literature estimate; actual yield depends on mouse age, strain, and protocol execution). Contaminating epithelial cells can be excluded in flow cytometry using EpCAM (CD326) in the dump channel.

text:
35% vs 37% vs 40–44% for IEL isolation
The Percoll concentration used for IEL enrichment varies across published protocols:

35% — used by some groups (including this collaborator protocol) as a single-density pellet-through. Lymphocytes pellet; many epithelial cells remain in the supernatant. Simpler but lower purity.
37% — the lab standard for liver leukocyte enrichment (BUF-PERC-37). Compatible with IEL isolation and can be used as a practical alternative to 35% without changing the isotonic Percoll stock preparation.
40–44% — more widely used in published murine IEL protocols. Higher Percoll density improves separation of lymphocytes from epithelial cells and increases preparation purity.
44%/67% discontinuous gradient — the gold standard in the most widely cited protocols (Lefrancois & Lycke 2001; Bhatt & Bhatt 2022). IELs are collected from the 44/67% interface rather than as a pellet, yielding 30–80% CD45+ purity. Requires underlaying 67% Percoll and more careful technique but gives the cleanest preparations.

Practical recommendation: Start with 35% (as in this protocol, matching the collaborator method). If purity is insufficient for your flow panel or gating (assess by EpCAM vs CD45 plot), escalate to a 44/67% discontinuous gradient.
