title: LCMV Viral Load Quantification by GP-Based SYBR Green qPCR
text:
Protocol ID: MUS-LCMV-QPCR
Version: v1.1
Author: Dillon Corvino

Purpose
This protocol describes a quantitative PCR (qPCR) assay for measuring lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) RNA in mouse serum and tissues, adapted from McCausland and Crotty, J Virol Methods 2008. The assay uses gene-specific reverse transcription with SuperScript III and SYBR Green qPCR targeting the GP segment, which provides improved specificity and sensitivity compared with NP-based assays.






WarningLCMV biosafety and handling



LCMV is a zoonotic arenavirus capable of causing severe disease in humans, including meningitis and congenital infection. Work with live LCMV must:

Be conducted under the appropriate institutional biosafety level (typically BSL-2 with additional local conditions) and approved animal and biosafety protocols.
Use dedicated infectious CO₂ incubators and clearly labelled containment for all cultures and waste.
Include suitable PPE (lab coat/gown, gloves, eye protection as appropriate) and measures to avoid sharps injuries, aerosol formation, and spills.
Exclude or take special precautions for pregnant or immunocompromised personnel according to institutional policies.

All waste (liquid and solid) must be inactivated according to local regulations (e.g. chemical disinfection and/or autoclaving) before disposal.






Principle

Total RNA is isolated from serum or homogenized tissue.
cDNA is generated using SuperScript III and a gene-specific primer (GP-R).
qPCR is performed with SYBR Green detection using GP-specific primers (GP-F and GP-R).
Absolute viral RNA copy numbers are calculated from a plasmid standard curve containing the LCMV GP gene (e.g. pSG5-GP).



Sample Types

Serum (typically 50 uL per sample).
Tissue homogenates:

Spleen: 10 mg
Liver: 50 mg
Kidney: 50 mg
Brain: 50 mg
Lymph node: 5 mg


All values are taken from the Methods section of McCausland & Crotty. Samples were snap-frozen on dry ice at harvest and stored at -80 C until RNA extraction.


Reagents and Consumables

LCMV-infected mouse tissues or serum.
RNAqueous Mini Kit (Ambion) or equivalent silica spin-column RNA kit.
SuperScript III Reverse Transcriptase (Invitrogen).
iTaq SYBR Green Supermix with ROX (Bio-Rad) or similar SYBR Green master mix with ROX passive reference.
Gene-specific primers (see below).
Plasmid standard containing the LCMV GP gene (e.g. pSG5-GP).
Nuclease-free water.
1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
0.2 mL PCR tubes or 96-well qPCR plates with optical seals.



Equipment

Tissue homogenizer (e.g. Tissuemiser or similar rotor-stator homogenizer).
Microcentrifuge (refrigerated).
Class II biosafety cabinet or laminar flow hood.
qPCR instrument capable of SYBR Green detection (e.g. ABI GeneAmp 5700 or equivalent).
Standard laboratory pipettes and filtered tips.
-80 C freezer.



Primers
All primer sequences are taken from the “LCMV viral load quantitative PCR (QPCR)” Methods section.
Recommended GP primers (optimized set):

GP-F (S 877–901):
CATTCACCTGGACTTTGTCAGACTC
GP-R (S 970–991):
GCAACTGCTGTGTTCCCGAAAC

Alternative NP-based primer sets (historical, not recommended for new assays):

NP2-F (S 2601–2623):
CAGAAATGTTGATGCTGGACTGC
NP2-R (S 2697–2720):
CAGACCTTGGCTTGCTTTACACAG

Use GP-F and GP-R for all new experiments unless you have a specific reason to reproduce NP-based data.


Primer Stocks

Prepare 100 uM stocks of GP-F and GP-R in nuclease-free water.
Prepare 10 uM working stocks for routine use.



Sample Collection

Serum

Collect whole blood via retro-orbital bleed under appropriate anesthesia (e.g. isoflurane).
Use heparinized capillary tubes.
Transfer to 1.5 mL tubes and centrifuge 20 min at 12,000 g, 4 C.
Aliquot serum (minimum 50 uL) and store at -80 C.

Tissues

Harvest tissues with sterile instruments.
Wipe instruments with 70 percent ethanol between mice and always process uninfected controls first.
For qPCR, immediately snap-freeze small tissue pieces on dry ice.
Store at -80 C.




RNA Isolation
Based on RNAqueous Mini Kit usage:

Thaw serum or tissue on ice.
For serum:

Use 50 uL serum directly in the kit lysis buffer according to manufacturer instructions.

For tissues:

Weigh 5–50 mg tissue into appropriate tubes.
Add lysis buffer from the RNAqueous kit.
Homogenize thoroughly with a rotor-stator homogenizer.

Critical decontamination step for homogenizer between samples:

Wash once with PBS.
Wash once with 10 percent bleach.
Wash once again with PBS.
Do not rely on ethanol + PBS alone; this was reported as insufficient to prevent cross-contamination.

Proceed with the RNAqueous spin-column protocol.
Elute RNA in 20 uL nuclease-free water.
Store RNA at -80 C until use.



cDNA Synthesis (Reverse Transcription)
Using SuperScript III and gene-specific priming:

For each sample, set up a 20 uL RT reaction containing:

10 uL RNA (from the 20 uL eluate).
1 gene-specific primer (usually GP-R at 0.5–1 uM final).
dNTPs (as supplied or 0.5 mM each).
Reaction buffer and DTT per SuperScript III instructions.
SuperScript III Reverse Transcriptase (as per manufacturer recommendation, often 200 U per reaction).

Incubate:

55 C for 60 min (50 C can also be used but 55 C is preferred in the paper for specificity).
Then inactivate at 70 C for 15 min or according to kit instructions.

Include:

At least two tissue-matched RNA samples from uninfected mice (negative controls).
No-template control (water instead of RNA).

Store cDNA at -20 C if not used immediately.



qPCR Reaction Setup
Standard reaction (25 uL total volume):

5 uL cDNA template.
12.5 uL iTaq SYBR Green Supermix with ROX (2x).
0.5 uL GP-F (10 uM; final 0.2 uM).
0.5 uL GP-R (10 uM; final 0.2 uM).
6.5 uL nuclease-free water.

Notes: - 50 uL reactions can also be used; scale reagents proportionally. - Prepare a master mix for all wells to minimise pipetting error. - Run all samples in duplicate.


qPCR Cycling Conditions
On ABI GeneAmp 5700 or similar:

Initial denaturation: 95 C, 3 min (or per master mix recommendations).
40 cycles of:

95 C, 15 s
60 C, 30 s (combined annealing/extension; fluorescence read step)


After amplification, perform a melt-curve analysis to verify a single specific product.


Plasmid Standard Curve

Use a plasmid containing the LCMV GP gene (e.g. pSG5-GP).
Linearize the plasmid with an appropriate restriction enzyme.
Quantify DNA by gel electrophoresis against known DNA standards.
Convert mass to copy number using molecular weight.
Prepare 10-fold serial dilutions covering the desired range (e.g. 10^7 to 10^0 genome copies per reaction).
Aliquot each dilution and store at -80 C (single-use aliquots).
In every run:

Thaw a fresh aliquot series.
Run each standard in duplicate.

Generate a Ct vs log10(copy number) standard curve; R^2 should typically be > 0.98.



Data Analysis

For each plate, fit a linear regression of Ct versus log10(copy number) using the plasmid standards.
For each sample, convert Ct to copy number using the standard curve.
Correct for:

Fraction of RNA used (10 uL of 20 uL).
Volume or mass of starting material.

Report viral load as:

LCMV RNA copies per mL serum, or
LCMV RNA copies per mg tissue.

Limit of detection:

The assay reproducibly detects approximately 1–5 LCMV genomes per qPCR reaction.
In practice, set a Ct cutoff at 35–36 cycles; values above this should be considered below detection limit or flagged as unreliable.

Use negative controls (uninfected tissue and no-template wells) to define background; any sample with signal overlapping control levels should be treated as negative.



Controls and QC
Include in every run:

No-template controls (water instead of cDNA).
At least two uninfected control tissue samples per tissue type.
A positive control cDNA sample from a known LCMV-positive tissue.
Full plasmid standard curve.

Check:

Single peak in melt curve for all positive wells.
No amplification in no-template controls within the Ct window used for positivity.



Notes and Tips

Work in a laminar flow hood where possible; use UV decontamination between runs.
Handle plasmid standards last and avoid placing them adjacent to unknown samples on the plate.
For very high viral loads, a 1:200 dilution of cDNA may be required to bring Ct values into the dynamic range of the standard curve.



Buffers Required
Full composition, preparation, storage, and safety information for each buffer lives in its own linked buffer document — only a concise per-buffer summary is reproduced here, generated automatically from that document.
None


Safety considerations

Confirm that all work with LCMV and infected animals/samples is covered by approved biosafety and animal use protocols.
Perform all live-virus manipulations (thawing virus stocks, infection steps, handling of unfixed plates) in a certified Class II biosafety cabinet.
Use dedicated infectious incubators and clearly label plates, flasks, and waste containers with the virus strain and date.
Wear appropriate PPE at all times (lab coat/gown, gloves, eye/face protection as required).
Decontaminate all liquid waste (e.g. with freshly prepared bleach) before disposal. Solid waste (tips, plates, tubes) must be autoclaved or otherwise inactivated according to institutional guidelines.
OPD and its solutions are handled as chemical hazardous waste; follow chemical safety rules in addition to biosafety rules.
Pregnant or immunocompromised personnel should not work with LCMV unless explicitly allowed under institutional policy with additional safeguards.

This maximises early virus-cell contact. The Cologne protocol avoids full aspiration — it removes only 5 mL and replaces with 5 mL containing virus, keeping cells submerged throughout.

text:
Freezing
Snap-freeze aliquots in a dry ice / isopropanol bath, then transfer to -80°C for storage.
To prepare the bath:

Add dry ice to a suitable container (e.g. a small polystyrene box or ice bucket — do not use glass or material that will crack at -78°C).
Crush or break the dry ice into smaller pieces to maximise surface contact.
Pour isopropanol (or 100% ethanol) over the dry ice until it covers the pieces. The bath will initially “boil” vigorously as CO2 sublimates — this is normal. Wait until bubbling slows before use (~1–2 min). The bath reaches approximately -78°C with isopropanol or ethanol; substituting acetone gives ~-86°C.
Submerge cryovials in the bath. Small aliquots (50–500 µL) will be solid within ~30–60 seconds.
Transfer frozen vials immediately to -80°C storage.







Warning



Use insulated gloves or forceps — the bath is -78°C. Work in a ventilated area or fume hood; isopropanol and ethanol vapour are flammable. Keep away from open flame.








Tip



Direct -80°C (Cologne approach): Placing aliquots directly into -80°C without a snap-freeze bath is simpler and used routinely in the Cologne protocol. Freezing rate at -80°C is slower (~-1°C to -5°C/min depending on vial placement and freezer load) but adequate for standard production runs where stocks contain 10% FBS as a cryoprotectant.








Tip



Controlled-rate alternative (Mr. Frosty): An isopropanol-based controlled-rate freezing container (e.g. Mr. Frosty) gives a defined -1°C/min rate — optimal for cells but unnecessarily slow for virus stocks and not recommended here.








Warning



Avoid repeated freeze–thaw cycles. Use multiple small aliquots and thaw each vial only once. Expect approximately 50% loss of infectivity per freeze–thaw even with FBS present.

title: Mouse Liver Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 1 – Preparation and setup

Pre-cool collection solutions

Pre-cool PBS on ice for liver perfusion.
Pre-cool MACS Buffer on ice for tissue collection and all subsequent washes.

Label collection vessels (choose one option per experiment)

Option A: 6-well plate collection

Label one well per mouse in a 6-well plate.
Add 3–5 mL ice-cold PBS or MACS Buffer per well.

Option B: 50 mL tube collection

Label one 50 mL conical tube per liver.
Add 5 mL ice-cold PBS or MACS Buffer per tube.


Label dissociation and processing tubes

Label gentleMACS C-tubes (or equivalent) for each liver.
Label 50 mL tubes for filtration, washing, and Percoll enrichment (one per liver).
Label 15 mL tubes for the post-lysis wash (one per liver).

Prepare buffers

Liver digestion buffer — BUF-LIV-DIG; 5 mL per liver.
37% Percoll working solution — BUF-PERC-37; 25 mL per liver (9.25 mL isotonic stock + 15.75 mL PBS). Add margin when preparing for several livers so the last tube is not short.
ACK lysis buffer — 1 mL per liver.
MACS Buffer for washes and final resuspension — allow ~110 mL per liver.

Warm digestion components

Pre-warm a water bath to 37 °C.
Place an aliquot of liver digestion buffer in the water bath to equilibrate.
If digestion buffer will be prepared immediately before use, pre-warm the base medium (DMEM, PBS, or HBSS) instead.

Equipment setup

Pre-cool a benchtop centrifuge to 4 °C.
Ensure access to a gentleMACS instrument with an appropriate liver dissociation program.

Items to take to the animal facility

Ice bucket with ice-cold PBS for perfusion.
6-well plates and/or pre-filled 50 mL tubes (as selected above).
Sterile scissors and forceps.
5–10 mL syringes (one per mouse or per treatment group).
Needles for liver perfusion (25–27 G recommended).
Absorbent pads and a waste container for perfusion runoff.

title: Mouse Liver Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 2 – Liver harvest and perfusion

Euthanise the mouse according to institutional and ethical guidelines (e.g. CO₂ asphyxiation or other approved method).
Place the mouse in a supine position and perform a midline incision to open the abdominal cavity.
Expose the liver and major vessels (Inferior vena cava and portal vein).
Load a 5 mL syringe with ice-cold PBS and attach a 25–27 G needle.
Perfuse the liver via one of the following routes:

Inferior vena cava

Portal vein

Slowly perfuse with ~5–10 mL ice-cold PBS per mouse until the liver visibly blanches.







Important



Perfuse with PBS or FACS Buffer only — do not perfuse with MACS Buffer.
MACS Buffer contains 2 mM EDTA. Anecdotal evidence suggests residual EDTA carried into the tissue inhibits downstream collagenase digestion (collagenases are Ca2+/Zn2+-dependent metalloproteases and EDTA chelates these cofactors).
MACS Buffer is fine for all subsequent steps — collection, washes, Percoll resuspension, quenching, and final resuspension.








Note



Efficient perfusion reduces blood content and improves hepatocyte removal, density separation, and downstream staining quality.








Warning



Handle needles and sharps carefully and dispose of them immediately into an approved sharps container after perfusion.



Excise the liver carefully, removing the gallbladder.
Place the liver briefly on filter paper to blot excess buffer.

title: Mouse Liver Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
section: STEP 3 – Liver collection, weighing, and mincing
text:
STEP 3 – Liver collection, weighing, and mincing

Transfer the perfused liver to a pre-labelled collection vessel (on ice).
(Recommended) Weigh the liver:

Briefly blot on filter paper to remove excess liquid.
Record the liver weight.

title: Mouse Liver Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 4 – enzymatic and mechanical dissociation

Option A - GentleMACS C-tube

Add 5 mL pre-warmed liver digestion buffer (with DNase) to a labelled gentleMACS C-tube.
Transfer the liver into the gentleMACS C-tube.
Secure the C-tube onto the gentleMACS instrument and place the warming sleeve over the tube.
Run the m_liver_02_02 program to mechanically dissociate the tissue.
After the program finishes, briefly inspect the tube to ensure the tissue has been mechanically disrupted into small fragments and is fully submerged in digestion buffer.
Run the HH17 program (~17 min) to allow warmed enzymatic digestion of the tissue.







Warning



Confirm that each C-tube is correctly seated and rotating before leaving the instrument.
If a tube is not spinning, stop the run, reseat the tube, and restart the program.








Important



Do not leave livers in digestion buffer beyond the programmed digestion time.
Over-digestion can strip surface epitopes and negatively impact downstream phenotyping.
Note: the gentleMACS instrument does not beep when the program finishes—set a timer before starting.


Proceed directly to STEP 5 – Filtration.


Option B – Manual mechanical dissociation (fallback)
Use this route if the gentleMACS is unavailable.

Add 5 mL pre-warmed liver digestion buffer (with DNAse) to a labelled 50 mL tube.
Transfer the liver into the 50 mL tube.
Using sterile scissors, mince the liver directly in the tube until fragments are approximately 2–3 mm in size.
Ensure all tissue pieces are fully submerged in digestion buffer and not adhered to the tube walls.
Place the tube horizontally on a 37°C shaking incubator (250 rpm) and incubate for 30 minutes.







Important



Ensure tubes are tightly closed and positioned securely on the shaker.
Set a timer — prolonged digestion can reduce viability and affect surface marker integrity.


Proceed directly to STEP 5 – Filtration.

title: Mouse Liver Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 5 – Filtration and washing
Applies to both Option A and Option B.

Seat a 70 µm cell strainer on a labelled 50 mL conical tube.
Pour the digested liver suspension through the strainer.
Using the back of a 5 mL syringe plunger, gently press the remaining tissue through the strainer until no visible fragments remain.
Rinse the strainer with ice-cold MACS Buffer while continuing gentle mechanical disruption.
Bring the total volume to 40 mL with ice-cold MACS Buffer.







Note



Filtration is performed directly into the 50 mL tube — no petri dish, and no dab/swirl recovery steps. One strainer per liver; do not reuse.



Centrifuge at 400 g for 7 minutes at 4 °C.







Important



Spin time depends on tube format. The longer path length in a 50 mL tube requires a longer spin to pellet equivalently:



Tube
Speed
Time




50 mL
400 g
7 min


15 mL
400 g
5 min



This applies to every 400 g wash spin in this protocol. Check which tube you are in before starting the centrifuge.



Discard the supernatant by pouring.
Resuspend the pellet and bring the volume to 40 mL with ice-cold MACS Buffer.
Recap and resuspend by inverting the tube back and forth, or with a brief but firm shake.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 7 minutes at 4 °C (50 mL tube).
Discard the supernatant and keep the leukocyte pellet on ice.







Warning



Cell pellets from digested liver are often loose and poorly compacted.
When discarding supernatant by pouring, do so carefully. Avoid flicking, shaking, or abrupt movements.








Note



Optional hepatocyte pre-clearing spin (recommended). A low-speed spin can be inserted immediately after filtration (before step 6) to sediment hepatocytes while leaving leukocytes in suspension:

Centrifuge at 50 g for 2 minutes at 4 °C.
Carefully transfer the supernatant (containing leukocytes) to a fresh 50 mL tube, avoiding the hepatocyte pellet.
Continue from step 5 above.

Why this is worth doing. Hepatocytes are large, fragile cells and rupture readily at the higher speeds used for the subsequent wash and Percoll spins. Lysed hepatocytes release DNA and cytoplasmic contents that drive clumping and trap leukocytes, and they release damage-associated molecular patterns — extracellular ATP, HMGB1, mitochondrial DNA — which ligate purinergic and pattern-recognition receptors and can activate the very leukocytes being isolated, altering activation-marker expression before staining. Removing intact hepatocytes at low speed first avoids generating that debris.
Weigh this against the leukocyte loss in the discarded pellet: a proportion of leukocytes will be carried down with the hepatocytes. The Percoll gradient alone removes hepatocytes effectively, so this step is optional — but it is recommended where activation phenotype is a readout, where clumping has been a problem, or for single-cell applications.

title: Mouse Liver Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 6 – Percoll enrichment






Note



The Percoll working solution is 37% of isotonic Percoll stock, which is the same solution as “33% Percoll” when quoted by final Percoll content (37 x 0.9 = 33.3). The AG Surace SOP #001 uses the latter convention. See BUF-PERC-37 — do not relabel one as the other without changing the recipe.



Aliquot 25 mL of 37% Percoll into pre-labelled 50 mL conical tubes (one tube per liver).







Warning



Use a 50 mL tube for the Percoll step, not a 15 mL tube.
In a 50 mL tube the hepatocyte layer floats clear of the pellet and the supernatant can be poured off cleanly.
If a 15 mL tube must be used, the hepatocyte layer sits much closer to the pellet — you must aspirate the supernatant under vacuum rather than pour, or hepatocyte contamination of the leukocyte fraction will be unacceptably high.



Using a transfer pipette, resuspend the cell pellet using the small remaining dead volume.
Take up approximately 1 mL of 37% Percoll from the corresponding 50 mL tube and use it to rinse the wash tube, resuspending any remaining cells.
Transfer the resuspended cells into the corresponding tube containing 25 mL 37% Percoll.
Repeat the rinse 1–2 times with additional small volumes of Percoll (as needed) to recover all remaining cells.
Recap and invert gently 2–3 times to ensure an even cell suspension.
Centrifuge at 611 g for 15 minutes at room temperature (20–22 °C) using:

Acceleration: high (e.g. acc 9)
Brake: minimal (e.g. br 1)








Note



611 g corresponds to 1700 rpm on the lab centrifuge (rotor rmax ~18.9 cm). If using a different rotor, set the instrument by relative centrifugal force (611 g), not by rpm. Equivalent speeds:

Warning



Avoid high brake settings during Percoll centrifugation. Abrupt braking can disrupt the gradient and reduce lymphocyte enrichment.








Important



Do not leave liver samples in Percoll longer than necessary. Prolonged exposure can reduce viability and negatively impact downstream applications. Plan spins and next steps in advance.








Note



After the Percoll spin, a hepatocyte layer floats on top of the solution, while a leukocyte + erythrocyte pellet forms at the apex of the tube.



Prepare a few layers of paper towel next to the waste container.
Pour off the hepatocyte layer and supernatant in one smooth motion.
Keep the tube inverted briefly and dab the opening on the paper towel to wick residual Percoll (avoid touching or dislodging the pellet).

Proceed directly to STEP 7 – RBC lysis. There is no intermediate wash.

title: Mouse Liver Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 7 – RBC lysis

Using a 5 mL or 10 mL Stripette, add 1 mL ACK lysis buffer to each pellet.
Using a transfer pipette, resuspend the leukocyte + erythrocyte pellet by aspirating and dispensing until homogeneous.
Incubate for 2 minutes at room temperature.
During the incubation, transfer each suspension into the corresponding labelled 15 mL tube.
At the end of the incubation, quench by topping up to 10 mL with MACS Buffer.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C (15 mL tube; return brake to a normal setting, e.g. br 6).
Discard the supernatant by pouring, dab the inverted tube on paper towel, and keep the pellet on ice.







Warning



Liver leukocytes are particularly sensitive to over-lysis. Do not exceed the stated incubation time, especially after enzymatic digestion or Percoll separation.








Note



HybriMax may be substituted for ACK (2–3 minutes at room temperature) and is gentler, but ACK at 2 minutes is the standard for this protocol.

title: Mouse Liver Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 8 – Final resuspension and counting

Loosen the pellet in the remaining dead volume by vortexing briefly.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL ice-cold MACS Buffer.
Count cells and assess viability (e.g. trypan blue) as required.
Proceed with downstream applications (e.g. flow cytometry, sorting, or culture of NLCs).







Tip



For flow cytometry staining, seed up to 5 x 10^6 cells per well of a 96-well U-bottom plate. This is the maximum recommended for a 50 uL staining volume — scale the staining volume up for more cells. Maximum well volume is 200 uL.








Tip



For single-cell sequencing applications, minimise the time from tissue harvest to final resuspension, keep samples on ice whenever possible after digestion, and consider additional debris/dead cell removal steps if yields permit.

section: Step 1 – Preparations on the day before sort
text:
Step 1 – Preparations on the day before sort

Determine:

Mouse genotypes (e.g. WT, CD160 KO, IFNAR1 KO, etc.).
Number of mice per genotype and per experimental group.
Number of timepoints and replicates for the proliferation assay.

Assign mice to the experiment in PyRAT (or equivalent animal management system) and record a cohort ID.
Export the list of mice and provide it to the animal facility (e.g. Kathrin) as required.
Prepare sort collection tubes:

For each sorted population (e.g. total NK, CD160⁺ NK, CD160⁻ NK), prepare 15 mL Falcon tubes.
Add 2–3 mL FCS to each tube.
Place tubes on a roller at 4 °C (cold room) or in the fridge overnight to allow coating.

Prepare 50 mL Falcon tubes with 1× PBS for spleen harvest:

One tube per mouse or per pooled group (as per experimental design).
Store at 4 °C until use.

title: In vitro NK Cell Proliferation Assay Using CellTrace Dyes
section: Step 2 – Preparations on the day of sort: spleen harvest
text:
Step 2 – Preparations on the day of sort: spleen harvest

Bring prepared PBS tubes and transport containers to the animal facility.
Remove cages of mice assigned to the experiment:

Pool mice in groups as required (e.g. groups of 10 within a cage).
Sacrifice mice (e.g. in CO₂ chamber) according to institutional guidelines.

Harvest spleens:

Place each spleen into a 50 mL tube containing cold PBS (5–10 mL).
Keep tubes on ice during transport back to the lab.

Refer to the relevant SOP for detailed organ harvest and splenocyte isolation, if needed.

title: In vitro NK Cell Proliferation Assay Using CellTrace Dyes
text:
Step 3 – Preparation of splenocyte suspensions

In a biosafety cabinet, transfer each spleen to a sterile Petri dish containing cold PBS.
Gently homogenise the spleen through a suitable cell strainer (e.g. 70 µm) using the plunger of a 5 or 10 mL syringe into a 50 mL tube.
Rinse the strainer with additional PBS to maximise cell recovery.
Centrifuge at ~400–500 g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in FACS buffer (BUF-MACS-BUF) or PBS, as appropriate for counting.
Count splenocytes and record total cell numbers.







Note



This buffer is referred to as “FACS buffer” in this protocol’s original prose, but its stated composition (PBS + 2% FCS + 2 mM EDTA) matches MACS Buffer (BUF-MACS-BUF), not FACS Buffer (BUF-FACS-BUF, which contains no EDTA). Referenced here as BUF-MACS-BUF to match the actual recipe used — flagging for a scientist to confirm which buffer was actually intended.








Note



A rough guideline used in the original SOP is ~1 × 10⁸ splenocytes per mouse. This can be used for initial planning but always verify by counting.

title: In vitro NK Cell Proliferation Assay Using CellTrace Dyes
section: Step 4 – NK cell isolation from spleen
text:
Step 4 – NK cell isolation from spleen
Follow the instructions of the magnetic NK cell isolation kit (e.g. EasySep Mouse NK cell isolation kit) and the recommendations for temperature and volumes.

Calculate the total splenocyte count and volume needed for isolation:

For example, if using 14 spleens and assuming ~1 × 10⁸ cells per spleen, plan for ~1.4 × 10⁹ splenocytes.
Adjust volumes and kit reagent amounts accordingly.

Adjust the splenocyte suspension to 1 × 10⁸ cells/mL in FACS buffer or kit-specified buffer at room temperature.
For comparison of NK cells from two genotypes (e.g. WT vs CD160 KO):

Perform complete NK isolation as per the kit instructions for each genotype (full recommended reagent volumes per mL of cells).

For experiments requiring NK subsets (e.g. CD160⁺ vs CD160⁻ NK from WT mice):

Perform a pre-enrichment step:

Use the same kit but with half the indicated volume of isolation cocktail and magnetic beads per mL of cells (to enrich but not fully deplete other cells).


Keep reagents, buffers, and cells at room temperature during the magnetic isolation, as recommended by the kit.







Warning



Deviating from the manufacturer’s temperature recommendations (e.g. performing kit steps on ice instead of room temperature) can substantially reduce NK cell yield and purity.



After isolation or pre-enrichment, resuspend NK-enriched cells in PBS for CellTrace staining (see Step 5).

title: In vitro NK Cell Proliferation Assay Using CellTrace Dyes
section: Step 5 – CellTrace staining of NK cells
text:
Step 5 – CellTrace staining of NK cells
This step uses CellTrace Violet (CTV) or CellTrace Blue (CTB) to track divisions.

Count enriched NK cells and calculate the volume needed for staining.
Resuspend NK cells at 1 × 10⁶ cells/mL in PBS (no FCS).
Prepare CTV or CTB according to the manufacturer’s instructions:

Reconstitute the vial in DMSO to create a concentrated stock.

Stain NK cells:

For CTV: use a final concentration corresponding to 1:5000 of the stock (as used in the original SOP).

For CTB: use a final concentration corresponding to 1:1000 of the stock.

Incubate at 37 °C for 15 min, protected from light.
Controls:

Before staining, remove aliquots of cells for:

Unstained control.
Live/dead-only control.

After CTV/CTB staining, remove an aliquot for:

CTV/CTB single-stain control.


Quench and wash:

Add complete NK medium (BUF-NK-MED; cRPMI with supplements and IL-15 omitted at this stage or added as per your lab practice) to a volume sufficient to quench the dye.
Centrifuge at ~400 g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant and resuspend in fresh NK medium or FACS buffer as required for subsequent surface staining.








Warning



Incorrect CTV/CTB concentration or prolonged staining can cause toxicity and alter NK cell behaviour. Always work within titrated ranges and avoid exceeding 15 min at 37 °C.

title: In vitro NK Cell Proliferation Assay Using CellTrace Dyes
section: Step 6 – Surface staining for sorting (if sorting NK subsets)
text:
Step 6 – Surface staining for sorting (if sorting NK subsets)
If sorting CD160⁺ and CD160⁻ NK subsets or other NK subsets, perform surface staining after CTV/CTB labelling.

Prepare surface staining master mixes in FACS buffer (BUF-MACS-BUF), including:

Fc block (e.g. 1:200).

Surface antibodies for NK identification and subset discrimination (e.g. NK1.1, NKp46, CD3, CD160, etc.).

Live/dead dye, if not already integrated earlier.

Stain up to 5 × 10⁶ cells in 50 µL surface staining mix per tube.
Incubate for 30 min at 4 °C, protected from light.
Add ~4× the staining volume of FACS buffer to wash.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min, discard supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet at 10–15 × 10⁶ cells/mL in PBS for sorting (e.g. for a 70 µm nozzle).
Prepare single-colour controls:

Single-stain controls for each fluorochrome in PBS.
Live/dead controls in beads and/or cells.

Keep all stained cells and controls cold (4 °C or on ice) and protected from light until sorting.

title: In vitro NK Cell Proliferation Assay Using CellTrace Dyes
text:
Step 7 – Sorting and collection

Set up the cell sorter (e.g. BD FACS Aria) with the appropriate nozzle (e.g. 70 µm) and sorting strategy for NK cells and subsets.
Use FCS-coated collection tubes prepared in Step 1:

Add an appropriate volume of NK medium (BUF-NK-MED) to each tube before sorting.

Sort NK populations:

For total NK proliferation: sort or gate total NK cells as required.

For subset proliferation (e.g. CD160⁺ vs CD160⁻): sort each subset into separate collection tubes.

Keep collection tubes at 4 °C or room temperature as appropriate and move them to the incubator as soon as sorting is complete.







Tip



Monitor sort purity and yield during the run to ensure that enough events are collected for the planned timepoints and replicates.

title: In vitro NK Cell Proliferation Assay Using CellTrace Dyes
section: Step 8 – In vitro culture and proliferation assay
text:
Step 8 – In vitro culture and proliferation assay

After sorting, count the NK cell populations (e.g. using a microscope or automated cell counter).
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min and resuspend in NK medium (BUF-NK-MED) supplemented with IL-15.

Add IL-15 to a final concentration of 100 IU/mL immediately before plating.

Plate sorted NK cells in suitable culture plates (e.g. 96-well U- or flat-bottom plates):

Typical seeding density: 20–50 × 10³ cells per well in 200 µL NK medium + IL-15.

Adjust based on yield and number of timepoints.

Culture conditions:

Incubate plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Include:

“Day 0” samples (can be fixed immediately after sorting).

Multiple timepoints (e.g. day 2, 3, 4, etc.).


Controls:

Unstimulated NK cells (IL-15 only).

NK cells with additional stimuli, if desired (cytokines, co-stimulation, etc.).

CTV/CTB single-stain and unstained controls (can be fixed early).

For each selected timepoint:

Harvest NK cells from the wells.
Optionally stain for additional surface markers (using standard FACS buffer and staining conditions).
Fix cells in 4 % PFA or Histofix as per your lab standard.








Note



The original SOP notes that Day 0 populations and single-stain controls can be fixed immediately for reference; subsequent timepoints should be acquired using the same cytometer settings as Day 0.

title: In vitro NK Cell Proliferation Assay Using CellTrace Dyes
text:
Step 9 – Acquisition and analysis

Acquire all timepoints on the same flow cytometer (e.g. Cytek Aurora) using:

The same voltage/PMT settings.
Consistent compensation and gating strategy.

When possible, use:

Counting beads and/or

A fixed acquisition volume and flow rate.

Analyse CellTrace dilution profiles for each NK population:

Determine the number of divisions.

Calculate proliferation indices and division indices as required.

Compare genotypes or conditions (e.g. WT vs KO, CD160⁺ vs CD160⁻).

title: Mouse Tumour Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 1 – Tumour excision and preparation

Euthanise the mouse using an approved method.
Expose the tumour and excise it with sterile scissors and forceps.
Remove fat, necrotic outer layers, and connective tissue using dissection scissors.
Rinse tumour briefly in cold PBS to remove blood and debris.
Transfer to a 10 cm petri dish containing cold PBS or FACS/MACS Buffer.







Tip



Remove necrotic regions; they clog strainers and reduce cell viability.

title: Mouse Tumour Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 2 – Mincing

On a sterile petri dish, mince tumour tissue into very small pieces using scalpels or scissors.

Aim for 1–2 mm fragments for optimal enzyme penetration.

Transfer minced tissue into a 50 mL Falcon tube containing 5 mL Tumour Digestion Buffer (BUF-TMR-DIG-v1.0).

title: Mouse Tumour Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 3 – Enzymatic digestion

Place tubes on a 37 °C benchtop shaker at 250 rpm.
Incubate for 30–45 minutes, depending on tumour density.
Every 10–15 minutes, remove the tube and gently shake or invert to encourage even digestion.







Warning



Over-digestion (>45 min) can reduce viability, especially in lymphocytes and myeloid cells.

title: Mouse Tumour Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 4 – Mechanical dissociation

Add FACS/MACS Buffer to bring total volume to 20–25 mL.
Pour the digested tumour onto a 70 μm strainer placed over a 10 cm petri dish.
Using the back of a 5 mL syringe plunger, mash the tissue thoroughly through the strainer.

Rinse the strainer with additional cold FACS/MACS Buffer until no visible tissue remains.
Transfer the filtrate back into a clean 50 mL tube.
Top up to 50 mL with cold FACS/MACS Buffer.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Carefully discard the supernatant.

title: Mouse Tumour Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 5 – RBC lysis (if required)

If the suspension appears red or contains substantial blood, add 1 mL 1× RBC Lysis Buffer (HybriMax or equivalent).
Mix gently and incubate for 3–5 minutes at room temperature.
Immediately top up to 50 mL with cold FACS/MACS Buffer.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant.

title: Mouse Tumour Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 6 – Final wash and filtration

Loosen the pellet by gentle flicking.
Resuspend in 5–10 mL FACS/MACS Buffer.
Filter again through a fresh 70 μm strainer to remove remaining debris and aggregates.
Keep the final cell suspension on ice for downstream applications.

title: Mouse Tumour Digestion to Single-Cell Suspension
text:
STEP 7 – Downstream applications
Proceed to:

Flow cytometry / TIL profiling

FACS sorting

Tumour microenvironment analyses

Cryopreservation of tumour-derived cell subsets

Single-cell RNA-seq / TCR-seq workflows

title: xCELLigence Real-Time Cytotoxicity Assay for LCMV-Infected Fibroblasts
section: STEP 1 — MEF culture and seeding for infection
text:
STEP 1 — MEF culture and seeding for infection

Background: MEF culture conditions
MEFs are adherent fibroblasts typically maintained in DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% P/S at 37°C, 5% CO2. However, for use in this cytotoxicity assay, MEFs are adapted to T cell medium (RPMI + 10% FCS + 1% P/S + 2 mM L-glutamine + 1% NEAAs + 50 uM beta-mercaptoethanol + 50 uM beta-mercaptoethanol) to match the effector cell environment. Adaptation is done by switching culture medium to T cell medium at least one passage (ideally two) before the experiment. All culture and assay steps in this protocol use T cell medium unless otherwise stated. Primary MEFs should not be passaged beyond P4-5, as proliferative capacity decreases. Cells are subcultured at 70-85% confluence — do not allow full confluence before passaging, as contact inhibition impairs subsequent growth.


MEF seeding density reference

Seeding density for culture/expansion: 2x10^4 – 4x10^4 cells/cm^2
T75 flask surface area: 75 cm^2 — seed 1.5x10^6 – 3x10^6 cells per T75 for routine passaging
Expected yield from a confluent T75: ~10x10^6 – 20x10^6 cells
Target density for infection (overnight approach): seed at a density that gives ~50% confluence 24-48 h later



Option A — Standard procedure (seed day before infection)

Aspirate medium and wash monolayer with warm PBS (1x).
Add 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA — for a T75 flask, add ~2-3 mL. For a 6-well plate, 0.3-0.5 mL per well.
Incubate at 37°C for 3-5 min. Monitor under microscope — do not over-trypsinize (reduces viability).
Neutralize trypsin by adding 2-3x volume of complete T cell medium (FBS inactivates trypsin).
Transfer to a centrifuge tube and spin at 300 x g, 5 min, RT.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend in complete medium.
Count cells using trypan blue exclusion.
Seed into standard 6-well plates or T25 flasks at a density that will yield ~50% confluence within 24-48 h. Infect the following day (STEP 2).







Note



For infection, cells should be actively dividing and at ~50% confluence — this is the optimal state for LCMV uptake. Avoid seeding into E-Plates at this stage; E-Plate seeding follows post-infection (STEP 2).




Option B — Same-day trypsin, replate, and infect (compressed timeline)
Use this approach when MEFs are already too confluent (>60-70%) on the intended infection day and there is no time to seed the day before.

Trypsinise as per Option A steps 1-7.
Count and reseed into 6-well plates. Seed at a density sufficient to achieve ~50% confluence within 4 hours — seed more cells than the overnight approach since proliferation is not relied upon to reach target density.
Allow 4 hours adherence at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Confirm attachment by microscopy before proceeding.
Infect immediately — proceed to STEP 2. The 1h adsorption step is unchanged.







Note



Same-day replating is acceptable when timeline constraints require it. MEFs adhere within 1-2 h and resume active metabolism within 3-4 h post-trypsin — viral uptake is not meaningfully impaired provided cells are confirmed attached and not blebbing.

title: xCELLigence Real-Time Cytotoxicity Assay for LCMV-Infected Fibroblasts
text:
STEP 2 — LCMV infection of fibroblasts
Timing: Infect when cells are at ~50% confluence (~24-48 h after seeding). Infection runs for 48 hours.

Virus preparation

Thaw LCMV-WE stock rapidly in 37°C water bath. Transfer immediately to ice.
Count cells in the wells to be infected, or estimate based on prior seeding density and expected doubling.
Calculate MOI and required PFU:
MOI (multiplicity of infection) is defined as the number of virus particles (PFU) per cell:

PFU required = MOI x number of cells
Volume of virus stock = PFU required / stock titer (PFU/mL)

Example: MOI 0.01, 4 x 10^5 cells, stock titer 1 x 10^8 PFU/mL
→ PFU required = 0.01 x 400,000 = 4,000 PFU
→ Volume of stock = 4,000 / 1 x 10^8 = 0.04 uL — dilute into adsorption medium to a workable volume (e.g. 0.5-1 mL per well)
Dilute virus in low-serum adsorption medium (RPMI + 2% FCS) to the calculated concentration.







Note



A MOI range of 0.01-0.1 PFU/cell is appropriate for LCMV infection of actively growing fibroblasts at ~50% confluence. MOI 0.01 has previously been used for this assay, which gives moderate infection rates and minimal cytopathic effect at 48 h — a reasonable starting point. Higher MOI (up to 0.1) will increase infection efficiency but may cause more target cell death before the assay begins.




Infection procedure

Remove culture medium from wells.
Add infection volume (0.5-1 mL per well for 6-well; scale accordingly): virus diluted in adsorption medium.
Add equivalent volume of adsorption medium (no virus) to control wells.
Incubate 1 hour at 37°C. Rock plate gently every 15 min to distribute virus evenly.
Remove virus-containing medium and wash wells 2x with warm PBS.
Add complete T cell medium (normal culture volume).
Incubate 48 hours at 37°C, 5% CO2. This allows viral protein expression and presentation on target cell surface.







Warning



All steps involving live LCMV must be performed in a certified Class II biosafety cabinet. Decontaminate all liquid waste with freshly prepared bleach before disposal. Follow institutional BSL-2 guidelines.

title: xCELLigence Real-Time Cytotoxicity Assay for LCMV-Infected Fibroblasts
section: STEP 3 — Harvest infected fibroblasts and seed E-Plates
text:
STEP 3 — Harvest infected fibroblasts and seed E-Plates
Timing: 48 hours post-infection.

Fibroblast harvest

Visually inspect wells under microscope — infected MEFs should appear morphologically intact but may show subtle changes. Significant cytopathic effect at this stage indicates infection was too high (reduce MOI).
Aspirate medium from all wells (infected and uninfected controls).
Wash once with warm PBS.
Add pre-warmed 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA (0.3-0.5 mL per well of a 6-well plate).
Incubate 3-5 min at 37°C. Monitor — do not over-trypsinize infected cells, which may be more fragile.
Neutralize with complete T cell medium (2-3x trypsin volume).
Transfer to 15 mL tube and centrifuge at 300 x g, 5 min, RT.
Resuspend in complete T cell medium and count. Assess viability by trypan blue exclusion — aim for >85% viability.



E-Plate background measurement

Add 50 uL complete T cell medium to each well of the E-Plate.
Place plate in xCELLigence instrument.
Perform background read to establish baseline impedance.
Remove plate from instrument and proceed immediately to cell seeding.



Target cell seeding into E-Plates
Choosing target cell number: Prior lab xCELLigence experiments (CD160, B16F10/MCA1956 targets) used 25,000 cells/well. However, given that effector cell numbers are limiting in this assay, reducing target cell number is desirable to keep E:T ratios achievable. Published literature supports lower seeding densities: an optimization study using porcine fibroblasts as targets found 7,500 cells/well generated a robust Cell Index within 10 hours (Galli et al., 2013, Xenotransplantation). A validated range for adherent targets in 96-well E-Plates across published xCELLigence cytotoxicity protocols is broadly 7,500-25,000 cells/well.
Recommended starting point for MEFs in this assay: 10,000-15,000 cells/well. This reduces effector demand approximately 2-fold compared to 25,000 targets while maintaining sufficient impedance signal. Validate CI at 24 h before committing to a final density.

Adjust cell concentration to the target density in complete T cell medium (e.g. 2 x 10^5 cells/mL for 10,000 cells/well in 50 uL).
Add 50 uL per well to E-Plate wells (total volume = 100 uL with background medium already present).
Assign wells:

LCMV-infected MEFs (effector wells + target-alone control wells)
Uninfected MEFs (effector wells + target-alone control wells)
Medium-only wells (background)

Allow plate to sit at room temperature in hood for 30 min — permits cell settling before scanning begins.
Transfer to xCELLigence instrument and begin scanning (every 15 min).
Monitor target cell adherence for 24 h before adding effectors.







Note



Target cells should reach a Cell Index of ~1.5-2.5 at the time of effector addition, corresponding to approximately 60-80% confluence. MEFs spread well and may reach this CI faster than tumor lines. If cells over-confluent before 24 h, reduce seeding density for future experiments.

STEP 4 — Effector cell addition and cytotoxicity assay
Timing: 24 hours after E-Plate seeding (once targets are 60-80% confluent).
Effectors should be prepared according to the appropriate isolation protocol and brought to the required cell concentration immediately before use. Examples of typical effectors for this assay:

NLCs sorted or enriched from liver of LCMV-WE infected mice, day 3 p.i.
CD8+ T cells sorted or enriched from spleen of LCMV-WE infected mice, day 7 p.i.


E:T ratio guidance
Published xCELLigence cytotoxicity assays using enriched NK or CD8+ T cells against adherent targets typically span 1:1 to 10:1 for sorted/enriched primary effectors, with higher ratios (up to 25:1–50:1) used for bulk mixed populations (e.g. splenocytes, PBMCs). For sorted NLCs or CD8+ T cells, the biologically informative range is generally 1:1 to 10:1; ratios above this are useful for establishing the assay ceiling but are not always necessary with potent effectors.

STEP 5 — Real-time monitoring
Monitoring parameters:

Data collection interval: every 15 min
Total duration: 24 h (extendable to 48 h)
Cytotoxicity typically begins 1-4 h post-effector addition

What to observe:

Stable CI in target-alone wells = healthy monolayer, assay running correctly
Decreasing CI in effector-containing wells = cytotoxicity
Rapid CI drop in Triton wells = expected; confirms instrument sensitivity

title: xCELLigence Real-Time Cytotoxicity Assay for LCMV-Infected Fibroblasts
text:
Cytotoxicity calculation
Standard formula adapted for impedance-based assays:
% Specific Lysis = ((CI_target - CI_experimental) / (CI_target - CI_maximal)) x 100
Where:

CI_target = Cell Index of target cells alone at each timepoint
CI_experimental = Cell Index of target + effector wells
CI_maximal = Cell Index of Triton X-100 treated wells (complete lysis)

text:

Export raw data from xCELLigence software.
Normalize Cell Index to the time of effector addition (t = 0).
Calculate % specific lysis at multiple time points (e.g. 4 h, 12 h, 24 h).
Generate dose-response curves: % lysis vs. E:T ratio.
Statistical analysis in R or GraphPad Prism.

Every run must include the following. These are non-negotiable for data interpretation:

title: Lab Naming and Versioning Guide
text:
Purpose
This document defines the naming conventions and identifier system used across the Corvino Lab protocol library. These rules ensure:

Consistency across all .qmd protocol and buffer files

Stable, human-readable identifiers

Clear separation of identity (protocol_id) from versioning (version:)

Scalable indexing as the repository grows

This naming guide governs all protocol, buffer, and supporting document files.




Identifier Principles
Each file includes a stable identifier (protocol_id) that never changes once assigned.
Document versions, however, reflect revisions and updates over time.
Identifiers are:

Human-readable

Hierarchical

Independent of filenames

Independent of version numbers




Identifier Structure
All identifiers follow this structure:
<DOMAIN>-<TOPIC>-<TYPE>-<ID>
Where:

DOMAIN
Defines biological context or system
Examples: - MUS → mouse
- HUM → human
- CELL → cell-line–based procedure
- GEN → general or cross-species workflows


TOPIC
Defines the primary experimental or biological theme
Examples: - LCMV → LCMV virology workflows
- PTPRC → genotyping or CD45 locus assays
- FLOW → flow cytometry
- RNA → RNA extraction or analysis


TYPE
A concise descriptor of the method class
Examples: - PROD → virus production
- PLA → plaque assay
- FFA → focus-forming assay
- QPCR → quantitative PCR
- GENO → genotyping
- PROP → propagation medium or cell maintenance
- MED → assay or experimental medium


ID
A three-digit number (001, 002, …) indicating discrete methods inside the same category.
Important:
The ID increments only when a new, distinct protocol or buffer is added—not when updating or revising an existing file.




Versioning
Versions are tracked exclusively in the YAML header:
version: "v1.0"

Version increases reflect evolutionary changes to the same protocol or buffer.

protocol_id remains unchanged across all updates.

Examples: - v1.0 → initial release
- v1.1 → minor modifications
- v2.0 → major revision
Never encode the version inside the protocol_id.



When to Assign a New ID (001 → 002)
A new ID is assigned when:

The protocol constitutes a novel method, not just a revision

The workflow differs in a functionally meaningful way

A buffer has a distinct formulation or different intended use

An assay variant is introduced (e.g., fluorescent plaque assay, alternate overlay formulation, new primer system)

Examples:

Virus Production

MUS-LCMV-PROD-001 → standard T75 BHK or L929 production

MUS-LCMV-PROD-002 → roller-bottle high-volume culture system



Assays

MUS-LCMV-PLA-001 → crystal violet plaque assay

MUS-LCMV-PLA-002 → fluorescent immunoplaque assay



Genotyping

MUS-PTPRC-GENO-001 → Ptprc SNP genotyping

MUS-PTPRC-GENO-002 → multiplexed three-primer allelic discrimination assay



Buffers

BUF-BHK-PROP → BHK propagation medium

Buffer IDs are BUF-{DESCRIPTOR} — no numeric suffix. One buffer_id maps to exactly one recipe/file; a serum-free variant would be a separate buffer_id (e.g. BUF-BHK-PROP-SF), not a numbered suffix on the same ID.




Filenames
Filenames describe the file content and follow this structure:

Protocols
prot_<domain>_<topic>_<method>.qmd
Examples: - prot_mus_lcmv_multi_strain_production.qmd - prot_mus_lcmv_plaque_assay_vero.qmd - prot_mus_lcmv_focus_forming_assay.qmd - prot_mus_genotyping_ptprc_jaxboy_single_tube.qmd


Buffers
buf_<target>_<function>.qmd
Examples: - buf_bhk_propagation_medium.qmd - buf_vero_propagation_medium.qmd - buf_lcmv_plaque_assay_medium.qmd




Required YAML Fields
Each .qmd file must include:
title:
author:
date:
version:
protocol_id:
Example:
protocol_id: "MUS-LCMV-PROD-001"
version: "v1.0"



Protocol ID Examples (Current Library)

LCMV Methods

MUS-LCMV-PROD-001 → LCMV multi-strain production protocol

MUS-LCMV-PLA-001 → Vero cell plaque assay

MUS-LCMV-FFA-001 → Focus-forming assay

MUS-LCMV-QPCR-001 → GP-based qPCR viral load assay



Genotyping

MUS-PTPRC-GENO-001 → Ptprc (CD45.1/2) allele SNP genotyping



Buffers

BUF-BHK-PROP → BHK propagation medium
BUF-VERO-PROP → Vero propagation medium
BUF-LCMV-PLA → LCMV plaque assay medium





Rules for Future Expansion

Maintain readability: avoid unnecessary abbreviations.

Keep identifiers short but descriptive.

Ensure no collisions within each TOPIC–TYPE group.

Do not remove or reuse IDs, even if protocols become deprecated.

Always update the version number when content changes.
